evidence.snippet: Consequently, OTULIN or A20-deficient cells have an excess of Met1 or K63 Ub chains on NEMO, RIPK1, and other target substrates, which lead to constitutive activation of the NF-kB pathway.
evidence.explanation: The mirror-image diseases. OTULIN and A20 deficiency remove the enzymes that take ubiquitin chains off the same substrates, and produce constitutive NF-kappa-B rather than deficient NF-kappa-B - which is what places LUBAC deficiency in a class defined by the direction of the ubiquitin imbalance, and is the main differential diagnosis to hold in mind.

hypotheses/0.description: Linear ubiquitin chains at receptor signalling complexes both enable canonical NF-kappa-B activation and hold the complex out of its death-inducing configuration. Losing them therefore produces immunodeficiency and autoinflammation from one lesion: the first through failed NF-kappa-B output in fibroblasts, B cells and T cells, the second through TNF-driven apoptosis and necroptosis of tissue cells. The model is supported in humans by the patient allele that removes the catalytic domain and produces both effects in the same cells, and in mice by the TNFR1 rescue of the endothelial and epidermal phenotypes.

hypotheses/1.description: The autoinflammation is driven not by cell death but by the paradoxical hyperresponsiveness of LUBAC-deficient monocytes to IL-1 beta, which the founding reports of both HOIL-1 and HOIP deficiency proposed. The mouse evidence pulls in the same direction: dendritic-cell-restricted Hoip deletion causes spontaneous inflammation that TNFR1 deletion fails to rescue and MyD88 deletion does. The two models are not exclusive and may operate in different tissues, but they predict different therapies - IL-1 blockade rather than TNF blockade - and no patient has been reported on IL-1 blockade.

open_questions/0.rationale: The two candidate drivers have evidence of different kinds pointing in different directions. For TNF: patient colonic mucosa carries markers of RIPK1 kinase-dependent death, TNFR1 deletion rescues the endothelial and epidermal mouse phenotypes, and anti-TNF therapy produces clinical responses in patients - complete in a SHARPIN-deficient patient, partial and non-durable in a HOIP-deficient one. For MyD88: in the dendritic-cell-restricted Hoip knockout, which is the model built specifically to ask this question about autoinflammation, crossing to TNFR1-null mice did not rescue the inflammation while MyD88 deficiency did, and the patient monocyte phenotype that both founding reports proposed as the basis of autoinflammation is IL-1 beta hyperresponsiveness, which is MyD88-dependent. The question is not academic: it decides whether IL-1 blockade should be tried in a patient whose fever breaks through anti-TNF, and no reported patient has received it.

evidence.snippet: However, we did not observe increased expression of TRIM25 in unstimulated HOIP deficient patient's PBMCs, compared to control cells (Figure S8).
evidence.explanation: The negative result that keeps this gap open: the TRIM25 route, which is the mechanism the literature proposed for LUBAC restraining type I interferon, was tested in a HOIP-deficient patient's own cells and not found.

evidence.snippet: At this point there is no strong evidence to categorize the HOIP deficiency as a new type I interferonopathy, and it is unclear whether these patients would benefit from treatment with JAK inhibitors.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement of the two open questions this gap records: the disease classification and whether JAK inhibition is indicated.

open_questions/1.rationale: Two unrelated patients with different genotypes carry an interferon-stimulated gene signature in blood, and a healthy carrier mother carries it too. The obvious candidate mechanism - LUBAC restraining type I interferon production by degrading TRIM25 - was tested in the second patient's PBMCs and TRIM25 was not increased. The signature appears to be T cell rather than monocyte driven, since excess STAT1 phosphorylation after interferon-alpha was found in naive CD4 and CD8 T cells but not in CD14-positive cells. Its therapeutic relevance is untested: no HOIP-deficient patient has received a JAK inhibitor, and the second patient's own authors decline to classify the disease as an interferonopathy on the available evidence.

evidence.snippet: Polyglucosan body myopathy with cardiomyopathy has been associated with mutations in RBCK1, a ubiquitin ligase, which have also been reported in children with early-onset immune disorder.
evidence.explanation: States the two-faced character of the RBCK1 disease - a muscle glycogenosis and an immune disorder from the same gene - which is the contrast this gap is about, since the HOIP patients show the immune arm without a comparable storage myopathy.

open_questions/2.rationale: Both diseases abolish LUBAC assembly, yet the polyglucosan arm tracks with the HOIL-1 lesion rather than with LUBAC loss as such. The founding HOIP report offers two readings and does not choose between them: either the storage phenotype depends on a HOIL-1 function outside the complex, or the HOIP L72P allele is simply not fully loss-of-function. The distinction matters for whether these are two presentations of one mechanism or two mechanisms sharing a complex, and it is also the point at which the boundary between this entry and the RBCK1 disease would be redrawn if the answer were the first one.

open_questions/3.rationale: Every constitutive Hoip-null mouse dies at midgestation from TNFR1-driven endothelial death, so the entire murine literature on this gene is about complete loss, while every reported patient retains residual HOIP. This is not a reason to discard the models - the TNFR1 epistasis they establish is unobtainable in humans, and the colonic caspase-3 and pRIPK1 staining in a patient shows the same route is active - but it does mean the quantitative relationship between residual HOIP and phenotype severity is unaddressed by any model. It is a live clinical question, since the four reported patients differ widely in severity and the one who died before two years old carried a nonsense allele.

steps/6.description: The one route into this entry that does not pass through the glycinergic synapse. ATAD1 encodes Thorase, an AAA+ ATPase that disassembles the complex between the AMPA-receptor-binding protein GRIP1 and the AMPA receptor subunit GluA2 and thereby controls postsynaptic internalisation of excitatory AMPA receptors. The reported biallelic allele locks Thorase in its oligomeric state, disassembly of the GluA2 complex is impaired, and knockout neurons expressing the mutant carry less GluA2 at the cell surface. The node is kept separate from the glycine receptor and glycine transporter nodes because the lesion is at the excitatory synapse, which is also why the clinical delineation study reads the resulting disorder as distinct from hyperekplexia.

Searched synonym-inclusive with `runoak -i ols:mondo search "GPHN"` (one hit, MONDO:0044792 large congenital melanocytic nevus, unrelated) and `runoak -i ols:mondo search "gephyrin"` (no hits), so this gene has no subtype row and no `subtype_term` to bind.

evidence.snippet: ATAD1 | ATPase family AAA domain containing 1 | hgnc:25903 | Disease-causing germline mutation(s) in
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists ATAD1 as a disease-causing gene for hereditary hyperekplexia.

evidence.snippet: clonazepam is the treatment of choice (95% found it to be efficacious).
evidence.explanation: The genetically confirmed cohort reports clonazepam efficacy in nearly all treated patients.

treatments/0.description: Clonazepam is the standard symptomatic pharmacotherapy for hyperekplexia, reducing excessive startle and stiffness in most treated genetically confirmed patients.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Clonazepam increases inhibitory tone symptomatically rather than correcting the causal gene defect.

evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence studies and surface biotinylation experiments demonstrated that the mutant protein is virtually absent from the plasma membrane.
evidence.explanation: Localises the defect to protein delivery rather than to catalytic activity alone, which is a different kind of loss of function.

steps/1.description: Biallelic SLC10A1 variants remove functional NTCP from the hepatocyte basolateral membrane. The mechanism is not only reduced catalysis: for p.R252H, functional studies showed markedly reduced taurocholic acid uptake and the mutant protein was virtually absent from the plasma membrane, so this is a trafficking or stability defect as well as a transport one.

evidence.snippet: The Na(+)-taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide SLC10A1 (NTCP) plays a key role in this process as the major transporter of conjugated bile salts from the plasma compartment into the hepatocyte.
evidence.explanation: Establishes NTCP's role in the cycle. It is this paper's background framing of established physiology rather than its own finding.

steps/2.description: The sodium-dependent uptake arm of the enterohepatic circulation is lost. It is not the only arm: sodium-independent uptake by the organic anion transporting polypeptides remains, which is why the cycle continues at all.

evidence.snippet: Importantly, the presence of secondary bile salts in the circulation suggested residual enterohepatic cycling of bile salts.
evidence.explanation: The inference is the authors' own and is stated as a suggestion, which is how this entry records it.

evidence.snippet: The identification of NTCP deficiency confirms that this transporter is the main import system for conjugated bile salts into the liver but also indicates that auxiliary transporters are able to sustain the enterohepatic cycle in its absence.
evidence.explanation: States both halves of the result: NTCP is the main importer, and it is not required to sustain the cycle.

evidence.snippet: Currently, organic anion transporter polypeptides (OATP) 1B1/1B3 were considered as the main molecular replacement mechanism, which were localized to the basolateral membrane of human hepatocytes and mediated the Na+‐independent uptake of bilirubin, bile salts and other organic anions.
evidence.explanation: Names the transporters behind this node and the property that makes them able to substitute: OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 take up bile salts sodium-independently, so they are unaffected by the loss of the sodium-coupled importer. The authors state it as established transporter physiology, citing three earlier studies.

steps/3.description: Secondary bile salts require intestinal bacterial modification and then return to the liver, so their presence in the circulation of an NTCP-deficient patient demonstrates that the enterohepatic cycle is still turning. Sodium-independent uptake by the organic anion transporting polypeptides is the presumed route. This node is why the disease has a laboratory signature out of all proportion to its clinical consequences, and it is the compensation that has to be invoked to explain the absence of cholestatic liver injury.

evidence.snippet: Bile salt synthesis and intestinal bile salt signaling were not affected, as evidenced by normal plasma 7α-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (C4) and FGF19 levels.
evidence.explanation: Excludes overproduction and disordered feedback as the source of the accumulation, which is what makes it a retention phenomenon.

evidence.snippet: The profile of bile acids (BAs) in the serum was significantly altered in these individuals and marked by both elevated proportion and concentration of primary and conjugated BAs.
evidence.explanation: Shows the abnormality is compositional as well as quantitative, in the adult cohort.

steps/4.description: The defining abnormality. Plasma total bile salts reached 1,500 micromolar against a reference of under 16.3 in the first patient, and in adults the serum bile acid profile is altered in composition as well as concentration, with both the proportion and the concentration of primary and conjugated species raised. Bile salt synthesis is not the problem: plasma C4 and FGF19 are normal, so production and intestinal feedback signalling are intact.

evidence.snippet: Hypercholanemia was observed in 99.12% of the patients.
evidence.explanation: The published frequency in the largest genotype-defined series.

evidence.snippet: Total bile salts in plasma were extremely elevated (up to 1,500 μM, ref. <16.3)
evidence.explanation: The magnitude in the index patient, with its reference interval. Quoted separately from the frequency because they are different claims.

steps/5.description:
Hypercholanemia is the defining abnormality and is close to universal — 99.12% of 113 paediatric patients. It is graded VERY_FREQUENT on that published figure rather than on an impression.
Read the near-universality against the ascertainment: patients in that series were identified by SLC10A1 genotyping, so the cohort is genotype-defined and the biochemical phenotype is not being used to select it. That makes 99.12% a penetrance estimate rather than a circular one.

evidence.snippet: Indirect hyperbilirubinemia in affected neonates exhibited higher positive rates in comparison to controls.
evidence.explanation: The case-control comparison. The source gives a direction and a comparator but no percentage, so FREQUENT is the band its "higher rates" supports without implying a number.

evidence.snippet: They both presented with neonatal indirect hyperbilirubinemia and remarkable hypercholanemia, and harbored the SLC10A1 variants c.800C>T (p.S267F) and c.263T>C (p.I88T).
evidence.explanation: Two genetically confirmed neonates with the presentation.

steps/6.description: Indirect hyperbilirubinemia is commoner in affected neonates than in controls. The source that first described it in two neonates is careful to call NTCP deficiency a possible contributing factor rather than the cause, and this entry keeps that hedge.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, transient cholestatic jaundice, elevated liver enzymes and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (Vit D) deficiency during early infancy were more commonly observed in patients than in controls.
evidence.explanation: The case-control comparison. No percentage is given; OCCASIONAL reflects that this is an early-infancy finding in a minority against a background where the cardinal biochemical abnormality is near universal.

evidence.snippet: but there were no clinical signs of cholestatic jaundice, pruritis, or liver dysfunction
evidence.explanation: The index patient had none of it at extreme bile salt concentrations. Recorded as REFUTE against the claim that cholestatic jaundice is a feature of this disorder, because it is the observation that keeps the phenotype from being overstated.

steps/7.description: Transient cholestatic jaundice in early infancy is commoner than in controls. The word transient is the source's and is what separates this from the persistent cholestasis of a genuine cholestatic liver disease — the index adult patient had no cholestatic jaundice at all despite bile salts at 1,500 micromolar.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, transient cholestatic jaundice, elevated liver enzymes and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (Vit D) deficiency during early infancy were more commonly observed in patients than in controls.
evidence.explanation: The case-control comparison for the enzyme elevation.

steps/8.description: Raised liver enzymes in early infancy are commoner than in controls, and like the jaundice they sit in the early-infancy window rather than being a persistent finding.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, transient cholestatic jaundice, elevated liver enzymes and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (Vit D) deficiency during early infancy were more commonly observed in patients than in controls.
evidence.explanation: The paediatric case-control comparison.

evidence.snippet: During the 5-year follow-up observation of 10 NTCP p.Ser267Phe homozygous adults, we found that the most common phenotypic features of NTCP deficiency in adults were hypercholanemia, vitamin D deficiency, bone loss, and gallbladder abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: The same finding in adults, which is what makes it the persistent feature rather than an infancy one.

steps/9.description: Vitamin D deficiency appears in both the paediatric and the adult series, which is unusual among the features here — most of the clinical associations are confined to early infancy. It is also the link the bone findings are hung on.

evidence.snippet: During the 5-year follow-up observation of 10 NTCP p.Ser267Phe homozygous adults, we found that the most common phenotypic features of NTCP deficiency in adults were hypercholanemia, vitamin D deficiency, bone loss, and gallbladder abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Bone loss among the recurring adult findings, with its denominator.

steps/10.description: Bone loss is among the four recurring adult findings. The denominator is ten individuals followed for five years, and the supporting mechanism is a mouse experiment in which the osteoporosis was induced by oestrogen withdrawal and aggravated by the knockout. No frequency is recorded because ten individuals in a single cohort does not support a band.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies showed that this mutation resulted in a markedly reduced uptake activity of taurocholic acid.
evidence.explanation: Measures the transport consequence of the patient's own variant, rather than inferring it from the variant class.

edges/1.description: NTCP is the major transporter of conjugated bile salts from plasma into the hepatocyte, so its absence from the membrane removes that route.

evidence.snippet: Total bile salts in plasma were extremely elevated (up to 1,500 μM, ref. <16.3)
evidence.explanation: The magnitude of the accumulation in the first patient, quoted with its reference interval so the scale is legible.

edges/2.description: Bile salts that cannot re-enter the hepatocyte remain in the plasma compartment.

edges/3.description: Losing the main importer reveals the auxiliary ones. This is the compensatory branch and the reason the disorder is not a liver disease.

edges/5.description: Indirect hyperbilirubinemia is commoner in affected neonates than in controls, and the source frames NTCP deficiency as a contributing factor rather than a cause. No mechanism connecting bile salt retention to unconjugated bilirubin is established in any located source.

edges/6.description: Vitamin D is fat-soluble and its absorption depends on the intestinal bile salt pool, which is the usual explanation offered. The located sources report the association, not the mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, the NTCP deficiency led to increased levels of serum BAs, decreased levels of vitamin D, and aggravated the osteoporotic phenotype induced by estrogen withdrawal in mice.
evidence.explanation: The chain measured in a knockout mouse. Note the osteoporosis was induced by oestrogen withdrawal and aggravated by the knockout, so the model does not show NTCP loss causing bone loss on its own - which is why the link type is INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES and why the accompanying discussion is typed HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH.

edges/9.description: The proposed route from the transport lesion to the bone finding runs through this node: bile-salt-dependent absorption of a fat-soluble vitamin fails, and the vitamin deficiency acts on bone. The knockout mouse measured all three - serum bile acids, vitamin D and the bone phenotype - in the same animals, which is what makes this a chain rather than three separate associations.

evidence.snippet: Sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP) is encoded by the gene SLC10A1 and expressed in the basolateral membrane of the hepatocyte, functioning to uptake bile acids from plasma.
evidence.explanation: The gene, its product, and its location and function. Background framing in this paper rather than its own result.

evidence.snippet: Having not been reported in any databases, the c.263T>C (p.I88T) variant demonstrated an allele frequency of 0.67% (1/150) in healthy controls.
evidence.explanation: The control allele frequency for the novel variant, which is the evidence offered for its rarity.

genes/0.notes:
Solute carrier family 10 member 1, encoding NTCP, expressed in the basolateral membrane of the hepatocyte. Biallelic variants cause this disorder.
NTCP has a second identity that matters here: it is the cell-entry receptor for hepatitis B and hepatitis D virus, and the dismech Hepatitis_D entry already carries SLC10A1 in that role. The same loss of function that produces the hypercholanemia would be expected to affect susceptibility to viral entry, but no source located for this entry tests that in NTCP-deficient patients, so it is recorded as a knowledge gap rather than asserted.

evidence.snippet: All NTCPD patients exhibited favourable clinical outcomes as a result of symptomatic and supportive treatment.
evidence.explanation: The outcome under supportive management in the largest series.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, over investigation and intervention should be avoided in the management of NTCPD patients.
evidence.explanation: The explicit recommendation against over-management, quoted separately because it is a distinct clinical claim from the outcome.

treatments/0.description: There is no disease-directed treatment. All 113 paediatric patients had favourable outcomes on symptomatic and supportive treatment, and the authors of that series conclude that over-investigation and over-intervention should be avoided — which in a disorder whose laboratory numbers look like severe cholestatic liver disease is an active clinical recommendation, not the absence of one.

evidence.snippet: Bulevirtide (BLV) is an entry inhibitor blocking entry of HBsAg into hepatocytes by interfering with the bile acid transporter Na+-taurocholate co-transporting polypeptide.
evidence.explanation: Establishes why the question is worth asking: a drug in clinical use for hepatitis D works by blocking the same transporter this disease abolishes, so bulevirtide treatment is the pharmacologic phenocopy of the genotype. Stated as the drug's established mechanism in the paper's opening rather than as its own finding.

evidence.snippet: BLV-induced increases in bile salts do not correlate with HDV RNA declines suggesting that the inhibitory effects of BLV on NTCP differ between blocking bile acid transport and hindering HBsAg entry.
evidence.explanation: Refutes the coupling the question assumes rather than the question itself. In 20 treated patients the rise in bile salts, the readout of blocked bile acid transport, did not track the fall in HDV RNA, so the authors conclude the transport-blocking and entry-blocking effects on NTCP are separable. Losing bile acid uptake therefore does not license the inference that viral entry is lost with it, which is why this entry records the resistance question as open instead of answering it from the receptor's identity.

open_questions/0.rationale: NTCP is the hepatocyte entry receptor for HBV and HDV, and the dismech Hepatitis_D entry already carries SLC10A1 in that role. A person with no functional NTCP is the natural experiment for whether receptor loss confers resistance, and the answer would bear directly on entry-inhibitor therapy. No source located for this entry reports HBV or HDV status in a genetically confirmed NTCP-deficient cohort. The question is recorded rather than answered because the inference is obvious and the evidence is absent, which is exactly the combination that invites an entry to overstate.

open_questions/1.rationale: The largest series ascertained patients by SLC10A1 genotype and compared them with controls, which is the right design and is why its findings are usable at all. But the clinical associations it reports — indirect hyperbilirubinemia, transient cholestatic jaundice, raised enzymes, vitamin D deficiency — are common conditions of early infancy, all reported as "more common than controls" without effect sizes in the abstract, and the index patient in the founding report had none of them at bile salt concentrations approaching a hundred times the upper reference limit. Distinguishing a consequence from a co-occurrence here needs effect sizes and replication in a second population, and this entry's frequency bands should be read as provisional until it has them.

open_questions/2.rationale: The human evidence is bone loss among the common findings in ten adults. The causal evidence is a mouse in which osteoporosis was induced by oestrogen withdrawal and then aggravated by the knockout — which supports a modifying role, not an originating one. Whether an NTCP-deficient person with no other risk factor loses bone is not addressed by either. The distinction decides whether these patients need bone surveillance or only the surveillance their other risk factors warrant.

evidence.snippet: The most prominent risk factor was hypertension, observed in 71% of mutation carriers with HCM and an additional risk factor.
evidence.explanation: Identifies hypertension as the dominant co-factor among affected carriers.

evidence.snippet: The MYL2 mutation c.64G > A on its own is incapable of triggering clinical HCM in most carriers.
evidence.explanation: States the dependence explicitly, which is what makes this a co-factor rather than an additive risk.

evidence.snippet: The co-presence of additional risk factors for hypertrophy such as hypertension, obesity, or other sarcomeric gene mutation increased disease penetrance substantially and caused HCM in 89% of MYL2 mutation carriers
evidence.explanation: Names obesity among the co-factors and gives the joint penetrance figure. Marked INDIRECT because obesity's own effect is not reported apart from the grouped co-factor analysis.

evidence.snippet: MYL2 mutated models of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may be useful research tools to study the molecular, structural, and energetic mechanisms of cardioskeletal myopathy associated with myosin RLC
evidence.explanation: Establishes MYL2/regulatory-light-chain variants as a cause of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an associated cardioskeletal component, in a transgenic model of the R58Q allele.

steps/3.description: The initiating lesion in CMH10 is a variant in MYL2, encoding the ventricular regulatory myosin light chain (RLC) that binds the lever-arm region of beta-cardiac myosin. In the common dominant form the variant is a missense change (archetype R58Q) incorporated into the sarcomere; in the rare severe recessive form biallelic loss-of-function abolishes normal RLC. Either way the lesion perturbs how the myosin lever arm transmits force and how the myofilament responds to calcium.

evidence.snippet: the R58Q mutation and not the N47K led to reduced RLC phosphorylation in Tg ventricles
evidence.explanation: Establishes the phosphorylation deficit in vivo and shows it is specific to the malignant allele.

evidence.snippet: A low level of maximal isometric force observed for R58Q- versus WT-reconstituted fibers was restored by S15D-R58Q.
evidence.explanation: Rescue by a phosphomimetic at Ser15 is what makes the phosphorylation deficit causal for the force deficit rather than a co-occurring finding.

steps/4.description: The regulatory light chain carries a conserved Ser15 phosphorylation site through which cardiac myosin light-chain kinase tunes force production. The R58Q allele lowers RLC phosphorylation in vivo, and this is allele-selective rather than a general property of HCM-associated RLC variants — the N47K allele, studied in the same transgenic series, did not reduce it. The deficit is mechanistically load-bearing rather than incidental: substituting an aspartate at the phosphorylation site to mimic the phosphorylated state restores force in R58Q-reconstituted fibres.

evidence.snippet: R58Q promotes the OFF state of myosin, both in reconstituted porcine fibers and in Tg mouse papillary muscles, thereby stabilizing the super-relaxed state (SRX) of myosin, characterized by a very low ATP turnover rate
evidence.explanation: Direct statement of the state shift this node represents, measured in two independent preparations.

steps/5.description:
Striated-muscle myosin partitions between an active force-producing state, a disordered-relaxed state whose heads can reach actin, and a super-relaxed (SRX) state with an ordered arrangement along the thick filament and a very low ATP turnover rate. R58Q shifts the equilibrium toward SRX in both reconstituted fibres and transgenic papillary muscle, leaving fewer heads recruitable. This direction matters clinically: the licensed cardiac myosin inhibitors for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy act by *increasing* SRX occupancy, so an allele that already stabilises SRX is not obviously the one that class was designed for. That reservation is a mechanistic inference, not a reported treatment failure, and is recorded as an open question rather than as guidance.
The ATP-turnover annotation on this node refers to the low turnover rate that defines the super-relaxed state itself. It is not in conflict with the raised actin-activated fibre ATPase reported for R58Q elsewhere in this entry: those are different measurements — the turnover of heads parked in the OFF state, and the enzymatic rate of the heads that are cycling.

evidence.snippet: a significant decrease in maximal contractile force and a significantly increased Ca(2+) sensitivity, both hallmarks of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-associated mutations in MYL2
evidence.explanation: States the two canonical functional consequences of HCM MYL2 mutations — reduced maximal force and increased myofilament calcium sensitivity.

evidence.snippet: Skinned SOL muscles and ventricular PMs of R58Q animals exhibited lower contractile force
evidence.explanation: Confirms reduced contractile force in ventricular papillary muscle of an R58Q RLC transgenic model, the in vivo correlate of the force deficit.

steps/6.description: The regulatory light chain stabilizes the myosin lever arm and modulates the calcium responsiveness of contraction. MYL2 disease variants reduce maximal contractile force while increasing myofilament calcium sensitivity — the two functional signatures repeatedly observed for HCM-associated MYL2 mutations. In transgenic RLC-mutant hearts and slow-twitch muscle, contractile force is lower than wild type, consistent with defective force transmission by the mutant lever arm.

evidence.snippet: The percentage of myofibrillar disarray and cells with irregular beating in MYL2-R58Q iPSC-CMs was significantly higher than that in control cells.
evidence.explanation: Reports the electrical instability of this node in human cells carrying the patient's own MYL2 allele.

steps/7.description: Patient-derived MYL2-R58Q cardiomyocytes remodel the calcium handling apparatus itself, with reduced L-type calcium current density, smaller and slower-decaying calcium transients, and a tenfold excess of irregular beating. This is a distinct lesion from the myofilament calcium sensitisation upstream: that one changes how the sarcomere responds to a given calcium signal, this one changes the signal.

evidence.snippet: The histological features of HCM include myocyte hypertrophy and disarray, as well as interstitial fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Names the defining tissue-level triad that this node represents.

steps/8.description: Sustained sarcomeric dysfunction produces the structural remodeling that defines HCM — cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, myofiber disarray, and interstitial fibrosis. RLC-mutant HCM classically involves mid-ventricular and papillary muscle hypertrophy, but the disarray-and-fibrosis substrate is shared with the other sarcomeric forms.

evidence.snippet: Skinned SOL muscles and ventricular PMs of R58Q animals exhibited lower contractile force
evidence.explanation: Measures the deficit in soleus and in ventricular papillary muscle of the same animals, which is the observation this node records. It establishes that the deficit exists in slow-twitch muscle; because the transgene is cardiac-restricted it does not establish that the allele acts locally there.

evidence.snippet: Myosin light chain 2 ( MYL2) gene encodes the myosin regulatory light chain (RLC) simultaneously in heart ventricles and in slow-twitch skeletal muscle.
evidence.explanation: States the shared expression that makes slow-twitch skeletal muscle a candidate direct target of a MYL2 allele, which is the human-side basis of this node.

evidence.snippet: even though R58Q expression was restricted to the heart of mice, functional similarities were clearly observed between the hearts and slow-twitch skeletal muscle
evidence.explanation: Refutes the reading that this model demonstrates the allele acting locally in skeletal muscle. The transgene is cardiac-restricted, so the soleus deficit it produces must arrive by a systemic route, and the authors flag the result as surprising for exactly that reason.

evidence.snippet: R58Q-mutant mice showed functional similarities between the cardiac papillary muscles and slow-twitch soleus skeletal muscle
evidence.explanation: A review restating the cardiac/slow-skeletal parallel, cited for the generalisation rather than for the primary measurement. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

steps/9.description: MYL2 encodes the regulatory light chain of heart ventricle and slow-twitch skeletal muscle simultaneously, and human pedigrees of light chain disease report cardiac hypertrophy together with abnormal skeletal muscle. Whether the skeletal deficit is a parallel local action of the allele or a systemic consequence of the cardiac disease is not settled, and the leading model argues against the simple parallel reading: in R58Q transgenic mice the soleus shows the same contractile deficit as ventricular papillary muscle and the fast-twitch extensor digitorum longus does not, but the transgene is cardiac-restricted, so the mutant light chain is not present in soleus at all. The authors present this as their surprising result rather than as evidence of local action. The human expression fact makes skeletal muscle a candidate direct target; the mouse experiment does not test it.

evidence.snippet: The presence of any sarcomere gene mutation was associated with a younger age at presentation (38.4 vs 46.0 years, p<0.0005), a family history of HCM (50.6% vs 23.1%, p<0.0005), a family history of SCD (27.0% vs 14.9%, p<0.0005) and greater MLVWT (21.0 vs 19.3 mm, p=0.03).
evidence.explanation: Places the MYL2 sarcomeric form within the familial, younger-onset, sudden-death-associated clinical pattern of sarcomere-positive HCM.

evidence.snippet: severely compromising the ability of myosin to develop contractile force and maintain normal systolic and diastolic cardiac function
evidence.explanation: Documents the severe systolic-and-diastolic failure of the biallelic infantile form.

steps/10.description: The remodelled, stiff, fibrotic ventricle produces the clinical endpoints of CMH10: diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, and a risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmia and sudden death. As with sarcomeric HCM generally, a positive family history of HCM and of sudden cardiac death is common. The severe recessive infantile form fails systolically and diastolically together and is fatal in infancy.

evidence.snippet: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetic disorder that is characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy unexplained by secondary causes and a nondilated left ventricle with preserved or increased ejection fraction.
evidence.explanation: States the defining clinical feature of the disease this MYL2 form manifests.

steps/11.description: Unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy is the defining feature; RLC-mutant disease classically involves mid-ventricular and papillary muscle hypertrophy.

evidence.snippet: severely compromising the ability of myosin to develop contractile force and maintain normal systolic and diastolic cardiac function
evidence.explanation: Links the MYL2 lesion to impaired systolic and diastolic cardiac function. Marked INDIRECT because the quote is a statement about myosin's contractile capacity in a reconstituted system, and the clinical echocardiographic phenotype follows from it by inference rather than being reported.

steps/12.description: Increased myofilament calcium sensitivity and a stiff, hypertrophied ventricle impair relaxation and filling.

evidence.snippet: severely compromising the ability of myosin to develop contractile force and maintain normal systolic and diastolic cardiac function
evidence.explanation: Supports heart failure as an endpoint, most severe in the biallelic form. Marked INDIRECT because the quote describes compromised myosin function and does not itself report heart failure.

evidence.snippet: A cardioskeletal myopathy with onset and death in infancy, morphological features of muscle type I hypotrophy with myofibrillar disorganization and dilated cardiomyopathy was previously reported in three Dutch families.
evidence.explanation: A human clinical source for cardiac failure as the fatal endpoint of the biallelic form, which the molecular quote above can only support by inference.

steps/13.description: Heart failure develops from progressive diastolic dysfunction; the recessive infantile form presents with fatal heart failure in the first months of life.

evidence.snippet: associated with a rare FHC variant defined by mid-ventricular obstruction and septal hypertrophy
evidence.explanation: States the mid-ventricular distribution for a named MYL2 allele. The evidence source is MODEL_ORGANISM because that is what this publication presents — it is a transgenic-mouse study — and the quoted clause is its background framing of the human entity it was built to model rather than a result it reports, hence INDIRECT. No primary human report of the A13T clinical phenotype could be located to cite in its place.

evidence.snippet: suggest that the mutations disrupt the stretch activation response of the cardiac papillary muscles
evidence.explanation: Locates the lesion at the papillary muscles in the original description of light chain disease, which is the anatomical basis of the mid-cavity pattern. Marked INDIRECT because the sentence gives the proposed mechanism at that site rather than reporting the hypertrophy distribution itself.

steps/14.description: The hypertrophy of MYL2 disease is not confined to the septum. The original description called the light chain form a rare variant of cardiac hypertrophy and located its lesion at the cardiac papillary muscles, without characterising an obstruction; mid-ventricular obstruction is attached specifically to the A13T allele in the later literature, and an apical distribution has been characterised for R58Q. Recording the distribution matters clinically, because a mid-cavity or apical pattern is what makes the diagnosis easy to miss on a study reported as normal septal thickness.

evidence.snippet: The mutation Glu22Lys was associated with moderate septal hypertrophy, a late onset of clinical manifestation, and benign disease course and prognosis.
evidence.explanation: Documents septal hypertrophy in a genotyped MYL2 family.

steps/15.description: The commoner distribution, documented in both of the MYL2 families identified in a systematic screen of the light chain genes. Notably it was moderate in both the benign and the malignant allele, so wall thickness did not separate them — onset age and sudden death did.

evidence.snippet: The percentage of myofibrillar disarray and cells with irregular beating in MYL2-R58Q iPSC-CMs was significantly higher than that in control cells.
evidence.explanation: Shows disarray arising in human cells from the MYL2 genotype alone, without the haemodynamic loading present in a patient's heart.

steps/16.description: Loss of the parallel alignment of cardiomyocytes, the pathognomonic lesion of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, is reproduced in human cardiomyocytes carrying the patient's own MYL2-R58Q allele — twice the rate seen in control cells.

evidence.snippet: The mutation Arg58Gln showed also moderate septal hypertrophy, but, in contrast, it was associated with an early onset of clinical manifestation and premature sudden cardiac death.
evidence.explanation: Directly associates the R58Q allele with premature sudden cardiac death in a genotyped family.

evidence.snippet: R58Q existed in all six members with HCM and two healthy juveniles who had not yet developed HCM yet, and presumably in three deceased members who suffered from sudden death
evidence.explanation: Independent pedigree evidence for sudden death in R58Q carriers, in a family large enough to show co-segregation rather than co-occurrence. The attribution to the three deceased members is the authors' inference from pedigree position, not a genotype result, which is why the sentence says "presumably".

steps/17.description: Premature sudden death is the outcome that separates the malignant from the benign MYL2 alleles. It was the distinguishing feature of R58Q in the family screening study that also identified the benign E22K allele, and a four-generation pedigree carrying R58Q recorded three deceased members who died suddenly. No denominator exists — there is no MYL2-stratified outcome cohort — so this is a documented association and not a quantified risk.

evidence.snippet: pathogenic and related to obstructive septal asymmetrical hypertrophy with a good prognosis
evidence.explanation: Attaches obstructive hypertrophy to a named MYL2 allele (D166A) rather than to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in general. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review reporting another group's cohort.

evidence.snippet: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is often associated with left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, which affects a substantial proportion of patients.
evidence.explanation: Establishes obstruction as a common manifestation of the disease class this entity belongs to, which is the basis on which the entry curates obstruction-directed treatments. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

steps/18.description: Dynamic obstruction of the outflow tract is the manifestation the entry's pharmacological and septal-reduction treatments actually target, and both curated trials enrol on it. It is not universal in this entity: the D166A allele is reported with obstructive septal asymmetrical hypertrophy, whereas the D166H pedigree was explicitly non-obstructive. So obstruction is allele-dependent here rather than a feature of MYL2 disease as such.

evidence.snippet: causing severe hypertrophy with atrial fibrillation and likely pathogenic but related to a good prognosis
evidence.explanation: Reports atrial fibrillation for a specific MYL2 allele in a screened HCM cohort. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review reporting another group's cohort, and INDIRECT because the clause describes the allele's phenotype rather than measuring an arrhythmia rate.

steps/19.description: Atrial fibrillation is reported for a named MYL2 allele (I158L) alongside severe hypertrophy, and is a recognised endpoint of the atrial loading that follows a stiff, poorly relaxing ventricle. No MYL2-stratified incidence exists: the one MYL2 pedigree reporting a rate is a research letter whose PubMed record carries no abstract, so that figure is deliberately not curated here.

evidence.snippet: A cardioskeletal myopathy with onset and death in infancy, morphological features of muscle type I hypotrophy with myofibrillar disorganization and dilated cardiomyopathy was previously reported in three Dutch families.
evidence.explanation: Describes the skeletal muscle pathology of the recessive form in the pedigrees whose genetic cause the paper then identifies as MYL2.

evidence.snippet: each of which are associated with a rare variant of cardiac hypertrophy as well as abnormal skeletal muscle
evidence.explanation: Records skeletal muscle abnormality alongside the cardiac hypertrophy in the dominant missense form, so the cardioskeletal reach is not confined to the recessive entity.

steps/20.description: Because MYL2 is the regulatory light chain of slow-twitch skeletal muscle as well as ventricle, skeletal muscle is a target of the same allele rather than a bystander. The involvement was recognised in the original description of light chain disease and is the defining feature of the biallelic infantile form, where type I fibres are hypotrophic and myofibrils disorganised.

evidence.snippet: The light chains stabilize the long alpha helical neck of the myosin head.
evidence.explanation: Names the structural role through which a regulatory light chain variant reaches the lever arm, which is what makes this edge direct rather than an association between two separately evidenced nodes.

edges/1.description: The abnormal regulatory light chain disturbs lever-arm force transmission and shifts myofilament calcium sensitivity.

evidence.snippet: the R58Q mutation and not the N47K led to reduced RLC phosphorylation in Tg ventricles
evidence.explanation: Attributes the phosphorylation deficit to the R58Q variant itself, and shows it does not follow from carrying any HCM-associated RLC variant, since the N47K allele in the same experiment did not produce it.

edges/2.description: The R58Q allele specifically lowers the phosphorylation of the regulatory light chain in vivo. This is a distinct consequence of the variant, not a downstream effect of the force deficit, and it is allele-selective.

evidence.snippet: each of which are associated with a rare variant of cardiac hypertrophy as well as abnormal skeletal muscle
evidence.explanation: The original description reports cardiac and skeletal abnormality together in the same patients. Marked INDIRECT because co-occurrence in a pedigree does not distinguish a shared direct target from a systemic consequence of the cardiac disease.

edges/3.description: MYL2 is expressed in slow-twitch skeletal muscle as well as ventricle, and cardiac and skeletal involvement co-occur in human light chain disease. The link type is UNKNOWN rather than DIRECT because the intermediate steps are genuinely undetermined: the only model that measures the skeletal deficit produces it from a cardiac-restricted transgene, so a systemic route cannot be excluded and local action has not been demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: We found that both R58Q and N47K show reductions in force compared to the wild type that could result in compensatory hypertrophy.
evidence.explanation: Makes the causal step explicitly: the measured force deficit is what the authors propose the hypertrophy compensates for. The claim is the authors' proposed mechanism rather than a demonstrated sequence, so this edge rests on an inference they state rather than on an experiment that followed force loss through to hypertrophy.

edges/4.description: Chronic sarcomeric dysfunction drives maladaptive structural remodeling.

evidence.snippet: the L-type Ca2+ channel (LTCC) (ICa,L) density at 0 mV was reduced significantly by 45.3%
evidence.explanation: Shows a change in the calcium handling apparatus itself in patient-derived MYL2-R58Q cardiomyocytes, which is a separate lesion from the myofilament calcium sensitisation modelled at the upstream node.

edges/5.description: Beyond the myofilament's own calcium responsiveness, MYL2-mutant cardiomyocytes remodel their calcium handling machinery, including a large reduction in L-type calcium current.

edges/6.description: This node is the tissue substrate of the entry's defining clinical phenotype.

edges/7.description: The commonest distribution the remodelling takes.

edges/8.description: The allele-dependent alternative distributions of the same remodelling.

edges/10.description: Septal hypertrophy narrows the outflow tract, and obstruction arises when that geometry combines with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve — hence known intermediates rather than a direct step. Obstruction is allele-dependent in this entity, not an obligatory consequence of the remodelling.

evidence.snippet: echocardiographic examination showed significant alterations in diastolic transmitral velocities and deceleration time only in Tg-R58Q myocardium
evidence.explanation: Measures the diastolic endpoint in the remodelled myocardium of an RLC mutant, and shows it separates the malignant allele from the milder one carried by the comparison line.

edges/11.description: The stiff, disarrayed and fibrotic ventricle is what impairs relaxation and sustains arrhythmia.

edges/12.description: The diastolic element of this node as an observable clinical phenotype.

edges/13.description: The heart-failure element of this node as an observable clinical phenotype.

edges/14.description: Impaired ventricular relaxation raises filling pressure and loads the atrium, and the resulting atrial remodelling is the substrate for fibrillation.

edges/15.description: The arrhythmic element of this node reaching its worst outcome. The link type is indirect with unknown intermediates because which patients with this substrate go on to arrest is precisely what no MYL2-stratified data answer.

evidence.snippet: R58Q promotes the OFF state of myosin, both in reconstituted porcine fibers and in Tg mouse papillary muscles, thereby stabilizing the super-relaxed state (SRX) of myosin, characterized by a very low ATP turnover rate
evidence.explanation: Reports the OFF-state shift in the same experimental system in which the Ser15 phosphomimetic reverses it, which is what connects the two nodes.

edges/16.description: Phosphorylation of the regulatory light chain shifts the thick filament away from the ordered, ATP-conserving OFF state; losing that phosphate shifts it back.

edges/17.description: Fewer recruitable heads is one of the routes by which the allele lowers maximal force, so this node feeds the force deficit rather than bypassing it.

edges/18.description: The clinical skeletal-muscle phenotype this contractile deficit corresponds to.

edges/19.description: Cellular electrical instability is a plausible contributor to the arrhythmic risk of this disease, but the step from an iPSC-cardiomyocyte beating irregularly to a clinical ventricular arrhythmia is not established, which is why the link type is indirect with unknown intermediates.

evidence.snippet: The co-presence of additional risk factors for hypertrophy such as hypertension, obesity, or other sarcomeric gene mutation increased disease penetrance substantially and caused HCM in 89% of MYL2 mutation carriers
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the joint effect on the hypertrophic outcome this node represents.

edges/20.description: Pressure loading acts on the same remodelling node the sarcomeric lesion drives, which is why the two combine to produce hypertrophy that neither reliably produces alone.

edges/21.description: Obesity adds haemodynamic load and metabolic drive to the same hypertrophic remodelling node, though the study reports it only within the grouped co-factor analysis.

evidence.explanation: ClinGen's Gene Curation Expert Panel classifies this gene-disease relationship as Definitive, which is the authority for curating the gene as CAUSATIVE rather than a candidate.

evidence.explanation: Characterizes the functional consequence of the biallelic loss-of-function allele class, which is the second, recessive arm of this gene-disease relationship and is distinct from the dominant missense arm.

genes/0.notes: Both the dominant heterozygous missense arm and the recessive biallelic loss-of-function arm are curated on this one gene record, because the gene-disease relationship is single and it is the allele class and dose that differ.

evidence.explanation: Documents that carrying a sarcomeric pathogenic variant, the class this entity belongs to, is what drives device implantation in practice in an unselected national cohort.

treatments/0.description: An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator provides primary or secondary prevention of sudden cardiac death in patients at high arrhythmic risk. The indication in this entry rests on the sudden-death association of the malignant MYL2 alleles; there is no MYL2-stratified risk model, so device decisions follow the general hypertrophic cardiomyopathy risk assessment.

evidence.snippet: The "2024 AHA/ACC/AMSSM/HRS/PACES/SCMR Guideline for the Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy" provides recommendations to guide clinicians in the management of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the guidance that governs pharmacological management of this entity. Evidence source is OTHER because a guideline is expert consensus over an evidence base rather than a study reporting its own data.

treatments/1.description: Medical management of hypertrophy, outflow obstruction, and heart failure symptoms follows standard HCM and heart-failure therapy. No MYL2-specific agent or genotype-directed regimen exists, and the guideline recommendations this entry inherits were not stratified by genotype.

evidence.snippet: Beta-blockers, including atenolol and nadolol, are considered the first-line treatment due to their ability to reduce heart rate and myocardial contractility and enhance diastolic filling.
evidence.explanation: States the first-line status and the mechanism by which it works. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

evidence.snippet: Conventional pharmacological therapies such as β-blockers and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are effective first-line treatments for obstructive HCM, and established invasive septal reduction therapies, such as surgical myectomy and alcohol septal ablation, provide effective relief of obstruction in refractory patients.
evidence.explanation: Independent review agreeing on first-line status and placing septal reduction after it in the sequence. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

treatments/2.description: Beta blockers are the first-line drug for symptomatic obstructive disease, reducing heart rate and contractility and lengthening diastolic filling. Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem) are the second-line alternative when beta blockade is ineffective or contraindicated, and disopyramide is added for refractory obstruction, though its side effects mean many centres use it as a bridge to septal reduction rather than as durable therapy. None of this is MYL2-specific; it is the disease-class therapy a symptomatic carrier receives.

evidence.snippet: Beta-blockers, including atenolol and nadolol, are considered the first-line treatment due to their ability to reduce heart rate and myocardial contractility and enhance diastolic filling.
evidence.explanation: Names diastolic filling as the thing the drug improves, which is the claim this edge makes. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Slowing the heart lengthens diastole, which is the mechanism by which beta blockade acts against impaired filling. The effect is INHIBITS because the node is the dysfunction, and the drug counteracts it; it does so by allowing more filling time rather than by improving intrinsic myocardial relaxation, which the sarcomeric lesion still governs.

evidence.snippet: Conventional pharmacological therapies such as β-blockers and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are effective first-line treatments for obstructive HCM
evidence.explanation: States first-line efficacy in obstructive disease specifically, which is the node this edge points at. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

treatments/2/targets/1.description: Reduced contractility lowers the dynamic gradient, which is why beta blockade is first-line specifically for the obstructive form.

evidence.snippet: Invasive septal reduction therapies (surgical myectomy or alcohol septal ablation [ASA]) can effectively relieve LVOT gradients in obstructive HCM, but these are targeted to anatomy rather than the genetic cause.
evidence.explanation: States both what the procedure achieves and the limitation that bounds it: it relieves the gradient without acting on the genetic cause upstream. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a narrative review.

evidence.snippet: Guidelines recommend optimization of medical treatment in obstructive HCM patients before proceeding to more invasive options such as septal reduction therapy (SRT)
evidence.explanation: Places the procedure after medical therapy in the treatment sequence.

treatments/3.description: Surgical myectomy or alcohol septal ablation relieves the outflow gradient in obstruction refractory to medical therapy. It is the procedure VALOR-HCM, curated in this entry's clinical trials, was designed to avert, so modelling the trial without modelling the procedure would leave the decision it addresses unrepresented. Note it targets anatomy rather than the sarcomeric lesion, so it acts on the obstruction phenotype while leaving every sarcomeric node upstream of it untouched.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: The procedure removes the septal muscle that narrows the outflow tract, so it acts on the obstruction phenotype directly while leaving the sarcomeric lesion upstream of it untouched.

evidence.snippet: Patients on mavacamten had greater reductions than those on placebo in post-exercise LVOT gradient
evidence.explanation: The pivotal randomised result establishing the class effect. Marked INDIRECT for this entry because the trial enrolled by phenotype and no MYL2 subgroup was reported, so the benefit is inherited from the disease class rather than demonstrated in this entity.

treatments/4.description: Mavacamten reduces post-exercise outflow gradient and improves exercise capacity and symptoms in symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and is the first disease-directed drug class for the condition. It is listed here as the class a symptomatic obstructive MYL2 patient would be considered for, not as a MYL2-validated therapy — the pivotal trials enrolled by phenotype and reported no genotype subgroup. There is also a specific mechanistic reservation for the R58Q allele, recorded in the discussions block: myosin inhibitors work by increasing occupancy of the super-relaxed state, and R58Q already stabilises it.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: The drug class acts on the same super-relaxed/disordered-relaxed equilibrium this node represents. The edge records that the target is shared; it does not assert that shifting it further toward SRX benefits a carrier whose allele already shifts it that way.

evidence.snippet: Patients on mavacamten had greater reductions than those on placebo in post-exercise LVOT gradient
evidence.explanation: A randomised measurement of the drug acting on this node specifically, which is a different claim from the molecular-target edge above and is why this edge carries its own citation rather than borrowing one. Marked INDIRECT for this entity because the trial enrolled by phenotype and reported no MYL2 subgroup.

treatments/4/targets/1.description: The measured clinical effect, as distinct from the molecular target above: the pivotal trial's primary haemodynamic result is a reduction in post-exercise outflow gradient. Recorded as a separate edge because the gradient can fall whether or not the drug corrects the primary lesion in a given allele, which is the open question this entry records for R58Q. The effect on this edge is INHIBITS while the molecular edge above is MODULATES: the drug demonstrably reduces the gradient, whereas on the super-relaxed-state node it shifts an equilibrium in the same direction the R58Q allele already shifts it, which is neither inhibition nor activation of that node and is the reservation recorded in discussions.

evidence.snippet: R58Q promotes the OFF state of myosin, both in reconstituted porcine fibers and in Tg mouse papillary muscles, thereby stabilizing the super-relaxed state (SRX) of myosin, characterized by a very low ATP turnover rate
evidence.explanation: Establishes the direction of the R58Q effect on the equilibrium the drug class targets, which is what raises the question.

open_questions/0.rationale:
The two facts are individually well supported and point in opposite directions. R58Q was shown to promote the myosin OFF state and stabilise SRX in reconstituted porcine fibres and in transgenic mouse papillary muscle, and the experimental intervention that improved the R58Q phenotype in that same work was a Ser15 phosphomimetic, which shifts myosin the other way, toward the disordered-relaxed state. Mavacamten shifts it toward SRX. If the R58Q lesion is an excess of SRX, the drug class licensed for this disease pushes in the direction of the lesion rather than against it.
Three things stop this being an argument against prescribing. Obstruction is a haemodynamic problem and a gradient can fall for reasons unrelated to whether the drug corrects the primary lesion. The SRX findings are ex vivo and in mouse tissue, not in an R58Q patient's myocardium. And no genotype-stratified data exist either way: EXPLORER-HCM and VALOR-HCM enrolled by phenotype and reported no MYL2 subgroup, so there is no reported failure of mavacamten in an RLC carrier to point at. What is recorded here is a mechanistic reason to expect the answer might be allele-dependent, and an experiment worth doing, not a treatment recommendation.
The corollary is that MYL2 is not mechanistically uniform. Sibling entries in this series carry the opposite lesion — the MYL3 A57G work describes inhibition of the super-relaxed state — so "sarcomeric HCM is hypercontractile" does not license assuming the direction of the SRX shift for a given light chain allele.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygous missense mutations in MYL2 are known to cause dominant hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; however, none of the parents showed signs of cardiomyopathy.
evidence.explanation: The unaffected obligate carriers are the observation that excludes haploinsufficiency as the dominant mechanism.

evidence.snippet: the R58Q mutation and not the N47K led to reduced RLC phosphorylation in Tg ventricles
evidence.explanation: Shows one of the entry's mechanistic nodes is allele-specific rather than a property of MYL2 disease generally.

evidence.snippet: The significant functional changes observed, despite a low level of A13T mutant incorporation into myofilaments, suggest a 'poison-peptide' mechanism of disease.
evidence.explanation: Names the dominant mechanism this discussion is weighing, and gives the observation behind it — disproportionate functional effect from a small mutant fraction, which is the signature of a poison peptide rather than of a dose deficit.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies revealed an abnormal A13T mutation-induced increase in isometric force production
evidence.explanation: The opposite sign of force change from R58Q, in the same protein and the same laboratory's transgenic system, which is the evidence that the functional signature is allelic rather than gene-level.

open_questions/1.rationale:
The recessive pedigrees settle a question the dominant literature cannot: the parents of children with biallelic loss-of-function MYL2 disease are obligate heterozygotes for a null-like allele, and they had no cardiomyopathy. So losing half the normal gene product does not cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and the dominant missense alleles cannot be acting by simple haploinsufficiency. The mutant light chain has to be incorporated into the sarcomere and do something there.
That much is settled. What is not is what the mutant chain does, and whether it is the same thing for every allele. This entry curates the functional signature that has been worked out for R58Q — the phosphorylation deficit, the SRX shift, the reduced force with raised ATPase, the calcium sensitisation — but the same-cohort comparison that made R58Q malignant made E22K benign, and the transgenic comparisons that isolate the phosphorylation deficit to R58Q show that N47K, an allele at a neighbouring residue, does not share it. Assigning the R58Q mechanism to MYL2 as a gene would overstate what has been shown.
The sharpest illustration is that the alleles do not even agree on the sign of the force change. R58Q lowers maximal isometric force; A13T raises it, and does so while incorporated into only about 10% of myofilaments — which is what led that study to a poison-peptide mechanism, the general shape of dominant action this discussion is asking about. A model in which a small amount of mutant light chain disproportionately disrupts the sarcomere accommodates both directions of force change and is consistent with the unaffected obligate carriers, since it requires the mutant protein to be present rather than the normal protein to be absent.

evidence.snippet: myosin light chain mutations are a very rare cause of HCM responsible for about 1% of cases
evidence.explanation: The rarity that explains why no MYL2-powered outcome cohort exists, and the only screened denominator this entry has.

open_questions/2.rationale:
Every quantitative clinical statement in this entry is either a single-family figure or a disease-class figure borrowed from unstratified hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cohorts. Sudden death in R58Q is documented as an association across two pedigrees with no denominator behind it; the only screened case fraction available is for the light chain genes as a class in a 186-patient cohort from 2002; and the guideline and trial evidence supporting the treatments block enrolled by phenotype with no MYL2 subgroup reported.
The gap extends to molecular data. A GEO search for MYL2-specific cardiomyopathy datasets returns nothing: the accessions that surface for MYL2 are studies in which it appears as a cardiomyocyte marker gene, and the accessions that surface for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are unstratified or concern other genes. That is why this entry carries no datasets block. Adding a generic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy dataset here would be the named-entity substitution the repository's dataset guidance warns about — relaxing the entry name to its parent disease — and the absence is the accurate record.
What would close it: a MYL2-stratified outcome cohort with a denominator, an allele-resolved penetrance estimate for R58Q comparable to the E22K founder work, and an isogenic-pair transcriptomic or proteomic profile of an MYL2-mutant human cardiomyocyte model.

evidence.snippet: The co-presence of additional risk factors for hypertrophy such as hypertension, obesity, or other sarcomeric gene mutation increased disease penetrance substantially and caused HCM in 89% of MYL2 mutation carriers
evidence.explanation: The quantified conditional-penetrance result this hypothesis is built on.

open_questions/3.rationale:
The founder cohort is unusually clean evidence for a model that is usually only asserted. Thirty-eight carriers of one allele on one haplotype: the allele alone was largely benign, and with hypertension, obesity, or a second sarcomeric variant, 89% of carriers had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The authors drew two conclusions that both follow from it — screen carriers for treatable hypertrophy drivers, and stop excluding hypertensive patients from genetic studies on the grounds that their hypertrophy is already explained.
Whether the model generalises is open, and the founder design cuts both ways: one haplotype in one population controls for genetic background beautifully and also means the result could be specific to that background. The disease-class penetrance literature is consistent with conditional penetrance without demonstrating it — incidentally identified population carriers of sarcomeric variants have much lower penetrance than clinically ascertained ones, which is what a model requiring a second driver predicts, but is also what ascertainment bias alone predicts.

steps/1.description: A hemizygous germline variant in SRPK3 (NM_014370.4) in an affected male, inherited from a heterozygous mother. Four missense variants are known - p.His159Asp in the first kinase domain, p.Ser318Leu in the unstructured spacer loop, and p.Thr458Asn and p.Glu529Lys in the second kinase domain - plus one frameshift predicted to truncate the protein (p.Tyr471Ter). The missense variants are not all alike: modelling and cell localization suggest p.His159Asp and p.Thr458Asn destabilize the protein, while p.Ser318Leu and p.Glu529Lys may be hypomorphic. Whether the disease is a loss of SRPK3 kinase function has not been tested directly, so no functional-impact category is asserted.

evidence.snippet: We found that the H159D and T458N substitutions can cause protein misfolding, because His159 and Thr458 are located in the interior of SRPK3 and their side chains play a structural role for the maintenance of the protein folding
evidence.explanation: Modelling prediction for the two buried substitutions.

steps/2.description: Structural modelling on the AlphaFold SRPK3 model places His159 and Thr458 in the protein interior, where Asp159 loses about half of the side-chain atomic contacts and Asn458 clashes with neighbouring aromatic residues, predicting misfolding. Glu529 is surface-exposed and its substitution is instead predicted to alter a protein-interaction surface. Ser318 lies in an unstructured loop that could not be modelled.

evidence.snippet: Fluorescence cytochemistry revealed that SRPK3 wild type, S318L and E529K variants were mainly expressed in the nuclei, while the H159D and T458N variants exhibited cytosolic localization
evidence.explanation: Direct observation of variant-specific mislocalization in HeLa cells.

steps/3.description: GFP-tagged wild-type SRPK3 and the p.Ser318Leu and p.Glu529Lys variants were mainly nuclear in transfected HeLa cells, whereas p.His159Asp and p.Thr458Asn were cytosolic. Shown by overexpression in a non-neural cell line only.

evidence.snippet: The repeat regions (RS domains) are polyphosphorylated by the SRPK and Clk/Sty families of kinases.

steps/4.description: Presumed reduction of SRPK3 phosphorylation of serine/arginine-rich (SR) splicing factors. No study has measured SR-protein phosphorylation in patient cells, in variant-expressing cells, or in the knockout zebrafish.

steps/5.description: Presumed disturbance of SR protein-dependent alternative splicing in the developing nervous system. steps/7.description: Reduced cerebellar tissue. In adult srpk3 knockout zebrafish the valvula cerebelli, a cerebellar region suggested to serve non-locomotor functions, was roughly halved relative to brain area, together with the nucleus lateralis valvulae. In patients, the family 2 proband developed rapidly progressive cerebellar atrophy in his early twenties, and the fetus had a small, dysplastic cerebellum. Whether the human cerebellar change is primarily developmental, degenerative, or both is not resolved; SRPK3 mRNA in human brain rises with age and is highest in the cerebellum.

hypotheses/0.description: The presumed mechanism, following from the known function of the SRPK family: reduced SRPK3 activity (from a truncating, misfolded or hypomorphic allele) leaves SR proteins under-phosphorylated, impairing their nuclear entry and splicing function, and the resulting splicing changes disturb brain development. Every step after the variant is inferred from SRPK biology rather than shown in XLID114: no phosphorylation assay, splicing analysis or target transcript has been reported. The same paper notes that SRPK2 acts in synaptic vesicle release, so a splicing-independent neuronal role is also possible.

evidence.snippet: it is conceivable that defective or absent phosphorylation activity of this kinase, in combination with a second deficient downstream target gene, could result in these, as well as other, disease phenotypes

evidence.snippet: We identified 40 males (from 25 families) carrying hemizygous deleterious variants in the X-linked SRPK3 gene. Of those, only the 31 patients who also carried cosegregating heterozygous TTN variants presented with a myopathy.

hypotheses/1.description: Proposed by the authors of the SRPK3/TTN digenic myopathy study, who found that hemizygous deleterious SRPK3 variants caused myopathy only with a heterozygous TTN variant, and suggested that the same kinase deficiency combined with a second deficient target gene could underlie other SRPK3 phenotypes, citing the intellectual-disability reports. If it applied to XLID114, it would explain the gnomAD males carrying p.E529K or truncating SRPK3 alleles. No second locus has been sought or found in XLID114 families, and the fetal proband's extra VUS in BAALC and LOC400499 are not evidence for one.

evidence.snippet: Although, further studies with phosphorylation assays are required to confirm this prediction
evidence.explanation: The authors' statement that kinase function was not tested.

open_questions/0.rationale: The pathograph stops at a presumed splicing defect because nothing has been measured beyond variant localization in HeLa cells. The authors themselves say phosphorylation assays are needed. SR-protein phosphorylation, RNA-seq splicing analysis in patient-derived neural cells or knockout fish brain, and identification of mis-spliced targets would each test a step that is currently inferred.

evidence.explanation: Truncating SRPK3 alleles in population control males.

open_questions/1.rationale: The XLID114 evidence is one truncating allele, in a fetus with other variants, and four missense alleles of which two seem hypomorphic. The SRPK3/TTN myopathy study reports 40 hemizygous males with deleterious SRPK3 variants, most truncating, and six gnomAD males with truncating alleles, without describing cognition in either group. Whether those males are cognitively normal would decide between a simple loss-of-function model, an allele-specific (for example misfolding or interaction-surface) mechanism, and a second-hit model. Checking cognition and brain imaging in the myopathy cohort is the most direct test.

evidence.snippet: Initially, we injected 200pg of WT SRPK3 mRNA into one-cell stage zebrafish embryo. However, we did not observe any swim bladder inflation in srpk3 KO zebrafish.
evidence.explanation: The attempted rescue failed.

evidence.snippet: Srpk3-null mice display a new entity of type 2 fiber-specific myopathy with a marked increase in centrally placed nuclei
evidence.explanation: The mouse knockout phenotype is muscular.

open_questions/2.rationale: Mouse Srpk3 is reported as muscle-restricted, while human SRPK3 is expressed in embryonic brain, retina and cerebellum, and zebrafish srpk3 in brain, heart and muscle. The mouse brain is not described in the published abstract, the fish lacks a corpus callosum so the most distinctive human imaging finding cannot be modelled, and wild-type human SRPK3 mRNA failed to rescue the fish phenotype, which leaves open how specific the fish phenotypes are. A neural examination of Srpk3-null mice and a stable rescue in fish would address the mismatch.

evidence.snippet: The p.I328, mutated in the affected individuals, is part of the hydrophobic core of PSMC1; therefore, it is expected that its substitution by the hydrophilic threonine will affect the collapse of the core and, as a result, the structure of the protein.

steps/2.description: Rpt2/PSMC1 is one of the six AAA+ ATPases that form the base ring of the 19S regulatory particle and provide the mechanical work of substrate engagement, unfolding and translocation into the 20S core. p.I328 lies within the hydrophobic core of the motor domain, so replacing it is expected to perturb the folded structure of the ring subunit. No biochemical measurement of ATPase activity in patient material has been reported, so this node is supported by structural prediction plus the in vivo rescue result, not by a direct assay.

steps/3.description: Reduced ubiquitin-dependent degradation through the 26S holoenzyme. This is the shared node of the neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies: lesions in the 20S core (PSMB1), the 19S lid (PSMD12) and the 19S base (PSMC1, PSMC3) all converge here. The deficit in this disease is partial - a complete loss of the orthologue is lethal in mice and in worms - which is why a viable human phenotype exists at all.

steps/5.description: Loss of proteostatic capacity in neurons, the node from which the clinical neurological phenotype is drawn. The step between them is not directly demonstrated, so every edge out of this node is graded INDIRECT.

evidence.explanation: Structural modelling locates the substituted residue in the conserved ATP binding and hydrolysis domain and predicts hydrophobic-core disruption.

edges/1.description: The substitution replaces a buried isoleucine with a hydrophilic threonine inside the AAA+ motor domain, so the primary consequence is on the fold of the ATPase itself rather than on its expression level.

evidence.snippet: Fruit flies in which we silenced the Drosophila ortholog Rpt2 specifically in the eye exhibited an apparent phenotype that was highly rescued by the human wild-type PSMC1, yet only partly by the mutant PSMC1, proving the functional effect of the p.I328T disease-causing variant.
evidence.explanation: A cross-species complementation assay in fly eye, not a proteasome assay in patient cells, so the loss of function is inferred from incomplete rescue.

edges/2.description: A partly non-functional motor subunit lowers, but does not abolish, the proteolytic throughput of the 26S proteasome. The in vivo rescue assay is what fixes the direction and the magnitude: human wild-type PSMC1 nearly fully rescued an Rpt2-depletion phenotype while the mutant rescued it only partly.

evidence.snippet: proteasome activity was reduced, and augmentation of insoluble ubiquitinated protein was observed.
evidence.explanation: Reduced activity and accumulated insoluble ubiquitinated protein were measured together after knockdown of the orthologue in flies, not in human PSMC1-mutant tissue.

edges/3.description: Substrates tagged for degradation are not cleared, so polyubiquitinated protein accumulates in an insoluble fraction.

evidence.snippet: Impairment of specifically ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation caused intraneuronal Lewy-like inclusions and extensive neurodegeneration in the nigrostriatal pathway and forebrain regions.
evidence.explanation: Impairing ubiquitin-mediated degradation in mouse neurons alone is sufficient to cause inclusion formation and neurodegeneration. It is a conditional null in adult mouse neurons, not the human hypomorphic allele in development, so the step is inferred.

edges/4.description: Neurons are the cell type least able to tolerate a fall in degradative capacity, having no route to dilute an undegraded burden by division.

evidence.snippet: We now delineate an autosomal recessive syndrome of failure to thrive, severe developmental delay and intellectual disability, spastic tetraplegia with central hypotonia, chorea, hearing loss, micropenis and undescended testes, as well as mild elevation of liver enzymes.
evidence.explanation: Reports the finding in the affected homozygotes. The intervening mechanism is not established, so the item is graded INDIRECT.

edges/5.description: Severe global developmental delay in all three siblings. The mechanistic step from reduced neuronal proteostasis to this specific finding is not demonstrated; the edge records the clinical association in variant-carrying individuals.
