evidence.explanation: Reports the finding in the affected homozygotes. The intervening mechanism is not established, so the item is graded INDIRECT.

edges/6.description: Severe intellectual disability in all three siblings. The mechanistic step from reduced neuronal proteostasis to this specific finding is not demonstrated; the edge records the clinical association in variant-carrying individuals.

evidence.explanation: Reports the finding in the affected homozygotes. The intervening mechanism is not established, so the item is graded INDIRECT.

edges/10.description: No affected individual achieved verbal communication at any age. The mechanistic step from reduced neuronal proteostasis to this specific finding is not demonstrated; the edge records the clinical association in variant-carrying individuals.

evidence.explanation: Reports the finding in the affected homozygotes. The intervening mechanism is not established, so the item is graded INDIRECT.

edges/11.description: No affected individual achieved ambulation at any age. The mechanistic step from reduced neuronal proteostasis to this specific finding is not demonstrated; the edge records the clinical association in variant-carrying individuals.

evidence.snippet: Ventriculomegaly was evident on MRI.
evidence.explanation: Reports the finding in the affected homozygotes. The intervening mechanism is not established, so the item is graded INDIRECT.

edges/12.description: Ventriculomegaly on MRI, without a structural malformation. The mechanistic step from reduced neuronal proteostasis to this specific finding is not demonstrated; the edge records the clinical association in variant-carrying individuals.

evidence.snippet: Brain MRI (V10 as a toddler; V2 at early adolescence) was normal except for global mild to moderate ventriculomegaly and broadened extra‐axial space.
evidence.explanation: Reports the broadened extra-axial space alongside the ventriculomegaly in the affected homozygotes. The intervening mechanism is not established, so the item is graded INDIRECT.

edges/13.description: Broadened extra-axial space on the same scans as the ventriculomegaly, the second half of one imaging observation of reduced brain parenchymal volume. The mechanistic step from reduced neuronal proteostasis to this finding is not demonstrated; the edge records the clinical association in variant-carrying individuals.

evidence.snippet: Homozygosity mapping combined with exome sequencing revealed a disease-associated p.I328T PSMC1 variant.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the gene-disease relationship and the mapping that produced it.

evidence.snippet: a total of six neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies have been described, involving the four subunits PSMB1/β6, PSMC1/Rpt2, PSMC3/Rpt5, and PSMD12/Rpn5
evidence.explanation: Confirms PSMC1/Rpt2 as one of the four proteasome subunits implicated in neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies, independently of the founding report.

genes/0.notes: PSMC1 (14q32.11) encodes Rpt2, one of the six paralogous AAA+ ATPases forming the base of the 19S regulatory particle. A single pathogenic allele has been reported, the homozygous missense c.983T>C p.(Ile328Thr). The gene is highly intolerant of variation (pLI 1, missense Z 3.95) and no homozygous loss-of-function allele is recorded in gnomAD, consistent with a hypomorphic rather than a null mechanism in this disease.

treatments/0.description: No disease-modifying or mechanism-targeted therapy exists. Management is entirely supportive: developmental and rehabilitative therapy, audiological follow-up, nutritional support for the failure to thrive, and management of spasticity. Proteasome inhibitors used in oncology act in the direction opposite to what this mechanism would require and have no role here.

evidence.snippet: was fully nonambulatory, fed through gastrostomy, with severe failure to thrive
evidence.explanation: The direct documentation that this intervention was used in an affected individual, which is what distinguishes it from the standard-of-care entries around it.

evidence.snippet: Abbreviations: n/a, data not available; PEG, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.
evidence.explanation: The legend of the per-patient phenotype table, which defines PEG as one of its recorded variables. It establishes that gastrostomy status was tracked for each patient rather than noted once; it is a legend and not a finding, so it is graded INDIRECT and carries no count.

treatments/1.description: Enteral nutrition delivered through a surgically placed gastrostomy tube. This is the only intervention actually documented in the affected individuals: the eldest was fed through a gastrostomy at 20 years, and the paper's per-patient table carries a PEG column, so percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy was recorded as a clinical variable for this kindred rather than mentioned in passing. It is symptomatic, addressing the caloric consequence of the feeding failure and not the proteasome defect.

evidence.snippet: was fully nonambulatory, fed through gastrostomy, with severe failure to thrive
evidence.explanation: Records the gastrostomy and the severe failure to thrive together in the same patient. The source does not report a growth response to feeding, so the benefit is inferred from the route rather than measured, hence INDIRECT.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Delivers calories by a route that does not depend on oral intake, so it mitigates the growth failure without altering anything upstream of it.

treatments/2.description: Physiotherapy for spasticity, contracture prevention and postural management in non-ambulatory patients, following general practice for severe neurodevelopmental disability rather than any disorder-specific protocol.

treatments/3.description: Speech-language therapy, in practice augmentative and alternative communication, since no affected individual has achieved verbal communication.

treatments/4.description: Occupational therapy to support adaptive functioning and daily care, given the severe global impairment and non-ambulation.

treatments/5.description: Audiological follow-up with amplification where indicated. Hearing loss was present in all three published patients and is a modifiable contributor to the communication phenotype. NCIT has no clinical-action term for hearing-device use, so the generic rehabilitation action is bound.

treatments/6.description: Counselling on autosomal recessive inheritance with a 25% recurrence risk per pregnancy for carrier couples, and on targeted prenatal or preimplantation testing once the familial variant is known. Particularly relevant in the consanguineous setting in which this disorder was ascertained.

evidence.snippet: Three of the 10 offspring of healthy consanguineous parents of Bedouin Israeli ancestry
evidence.explanation: States the size and structure of the entire evidence base for this entity.

open_questions/0.rationale: The entity rests on three affected siblings of one Bedouin Israeli family. Every available proportion is a 3/3 or 2/3 count from that sibship, so no feature can be separated from the shared genetic background or from consanguinity-associated homozygosity elsewhere in the genome. This is why no frequency band is asserted on any phenotype in this entry. The source itself flags two findings in one patient - a duplicated renal collecting system and a muscular ventricular septal defect - as possibly unrelated to the PSMC1 variant, and those are deliberately not curated as phenotypes here.

evidence.snippet: Knock‐out of the PSMC1 ortholog in mice was shown to be embryonic lethal.
evidence.explanation: States the constraint that shapes the modelling problem: complete loss of the orthologue is embryonic lethal in mice.

open_questions/1.rationale: Two model systems support this entry and each is mismatched in a different way. The Drosophila assay is a knockdown of the orthologue read out in the compound eye; it establishes that p.I328T is hypomorphic, but says nothing about neurodevelopment. The mouse is a conditional null in defined postnatal neuronal populations that produces adult neurodegeneration with Lewy-like inclusions - a Parkinson-disease phenotype - whereas the human disease is congenital, static and not reported to be degenerative. Between them they support the molecular chain and the neuronal-dependence step; neither supports the developmental step, and the germline mouse null is embryonic lethal, so the disease genotype cannot simply be made in mouse by deletion.

evidence.snippet: The ambiguous genitalia with micropenis, undescended testes and low testosterone levels seen with the PSMC1 variant is unique and has not been reported in any of the diseases due to mutations in components of the proteasome.
evidence.explanation: States the observation that raises the question: this feature has no counterpart in the rest of the disease class.

open_questions/2.rationale: Micropenis with undescended testes, low testosterone and low gonadotropins was present in all three patients, with normal pituitary structure, normal remaining anterior pituitary axes, and normal karyotype and SRY. The source states that this is unique within the proteasomopathies. It is therefore either a genuinely PSMC1-specific consequence, or a feature of this kindred's background - and with one family there is no way to tell. Both Micropenis and Cryptorchidism are left unwired in the pathograph for this reason.

evidence.snippet: participants gaining 0.9 ± 0.3 kg (p = 0.009) during the ultra-processed diet and losing 0.9 ± 0.3 kg (p = 0.007) during the unprocessed diet
evidence.explanation: Inpatient randomized crossover trial with diets matched for presented calories, energy density, macronutrients, sugar, sodium and fibre -- so the 508 kcal/day excess intake and the weight change are attributable to processing itself rather than to nutrient composition. This is the strongest available design for the annotation claim.

evidence.snippet: the number of and distance to unhealthy food outlets increased the likelihood of fast-food consumption and higher BMI for children of any SES
evidence.explanation: Systematic review restricted to causal-inference studies. PARTIAL on two counts: the BMI effect is established for children of any socioeconomic status but among adults only for selected groups (females, black and Hispanic residents of low and medium density areas), and the marketing component of this annotation is not covered.

evidence.snippet: Under various physiological or pathological conditions, adipose tissue shifts cellular composition, lipid storage, and organelle dynamics to respond to the stress; this remodeling is called "adipose tissue plasticity".
evidence.explanation: Describes the dynamic remodeling of adipose tissue in response to obesity, including changes in cellular composition and metabolic function.

evidence.snippet: Histologically, there is evidence of significant infiltration of macrophages, but not neutrophils and lymphocytes, into WAT of obese mice, with signs of adipocyte lipolysis and formation of multinucleate giant cells.
evidence.explanation: Provides histological evidence of macrophage infiltration into dysfunctional adipose tissue in obesity.

evidence.snippet: These data suggest that macrophages in WAT play an active role in morbid obesity and that macrophage-related inflammatory activities may contribute to the pathogenesis of obesity-induced insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the causal role of adipose tissue macrophages in obesity-related metabolic dysfunction.

steps/6.description: Expanded adipose tissue becomes dysfunctional with increased inflammation, altered adipokine secretion, and impaired metabolic function. Adipocyte hypertrophy leads to hypoxia and macrophage infiltration.

evidence.snippet: Leptin acts through its receptor LepRb, expressed mainly in the hypothalamus, and induces a negative energy balance by potent inhibition of feeding and activation of energy expenditure.
evidence.explanation: Describes the central hypothalamic mechanism by which leptin normally regulates energy balance.

evidence.snippet: However, the majority of patients with obesity presents elevated leptin production, suggesting that in this setting leptin is ineffective in the regulation of energy balance.
evidence.explanation: Explains leptin resistance in obesity where elevated leptin fails to regulate energy balance through hypothalamic circuits.

evidence.snippet: Rare homozygous or biallelic variants in POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR can disrupt signaling through the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) pathway, resulting in hyperphagia and severe early-onset obesity.
evidence.explanation: Supports binding POMC and MC4R to this node: the melanocortin-4 receptor pathway is the hypothalamic circuit whose failure produces hyperphagia, and biallelic defects in it are the clearest demonstration of that circuit's role in human appetite regulation.

evidence.snippet: Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)-derived peptides act on neurons expressing the Melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) to reduce body weight.
evidence.explanation: States the POMC-to-MC4R step of the circuit this node represents, which is why both genes are bound here. Graded BACKGROUND because the sentence is the framing of a setmelanotide trial rather than that trial's own result.

steps/7.description: Central appetite regulation becomes impaired with leptin resistance and altered reward signaling, perpetuating overeating despite adequate energy stores. Hypothalamic neuroinflammation involves microglial and astrocyte activation that impairs melanocortin signaling. The genes bound to this node are the ones whose disruption is known to produce this state: leptin and its hypothalamic receptor LepRb set the afferent arm, and the melanocortin-4 receptor pathway downstream of it is the arm whose disruption produces hyperphagia. In common obesity these genes act as susceptibility rather than as sufficient causes; the monogenic diseases in which they are sufficient are curated separately (see notes).

evidence.snippet: Here we show that high-fat diet (HFD) feeding causes mitochondrial fragmentation in inguinal white adipocytes from male mice, leading to reduced oxidative capacity by a process dependent on the small GTPase RalA.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that obesity causes mitochondrial fragmentation through RalA in white adipocytes.

evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, RalA increases fission in adipocytes by reversing the inhibitory Ser637 phosphorylation of the fission protein Drp1, leading to more mitochondrial fragmentation.
evidence.explanation: Describes the molecular mechanism by which RalA promotes mitochondrial fission through DRP1 dephosphorylation.

evidence.snippet: Adipose tissue expression of the human homolog of Drp1, DNM1L, is positively correlated with obesity and insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Provides human evidence linking DNM1L expression to obesity and insulin resistance.

steps/8.description: Obesity causes mitochondrial fragmentation in white adipocytes through RalA-mediated activation of the fission protein DRP1 (DNM1L). This leads to reduced oxidative capacity and contributes to weight gain and insulin resistance. Mitochondrial dynamics shift toward excessive fission.

evidence.snippet: This study demonstrated that the abundance of A. muciniphila decreased in obese and type 2 diabetic mice.
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement showing the symbiont is depleted in obese and diabetic animals.

evidence.snippet: In humans, studies have provided evidence for a negative correlation between Akkermansia muciniphila abundance and overweight, obesity, untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus or hypertension
evidence.explanation: States the human cohort evidence for depletion in obesity. The quoted sentence is this trial report's summary of prior human studies rather than its own measurement, hence quote_role BACKGROUND; the correlation is also cross-sectional, so it bears on the depletion claim only indirectly.

evidence.snippet: The abundance of A. muciniphila is severely reduced in several pathological conditions (i.e., obesity, type 2 diabetes, inflammatory bowel diseases, and appendicitis).
evidence.explanation: Restates the human disease-state depletion across conditions. Quoted from the introduction of a mouse study, so the paper is MODEL_ORGANISM work but the sentence reports the human clinical picture.

steps/9.description: Akkermansia muciniphila is a mucin-degrading symbiont of the colonic mucus layer that uses host-derived mucus as its primary carbon and nitrogen source, placing it directly at the host-microbe interface. Its relative abundance is reduced in obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome and correlates inversely with body weight in rodents and humans. Loss of this population removes a signal that supports mucus-layer thickness and epithelial barrier integrity, and is the state that A. muciniphila-directed interventions are designed to compensate for.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrated that A. muciniphila treatment reversed high-fat diet-induced metabolic disorders, including fat-mass gain, metabolic endotoxemia, adipose tissue inflammation, and insulin resistance
evidence.explanation: The barrier/endotoxemia step is inferred from the therapeutic result: restoring the symbiont reverses metabolic endotoxemia and adipose inflammation in mice. Graded INDIRECT because the claim follows from the response to treatment rather than from a measurement of the untreated mechanism.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrated that Amuc_1100, a specific protein isolated from the outer membrane of A. muciniphila, interacts with Toll-like receptor 2, is stable at temperatures used for pasteurization, improves the gut barrier and partly recapitulates the beneficial effects of the bacterium.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the molecular route from the symbiont to barrier function, and the thermostability that makes a pasteurized preparation plausible.

steps/10.description: Thinning of the colonic mucus layer and loss of epithelial barrier integrity allow bacterial lipopolysaccharide to reach the systemic circulation, producing the low-grade endotoxemia that couples the gut to adipose inflammation and insulin resistance. A. muciniphila supports barrier function at least partly through its abundant outer-membrane protein Amuc_1100, a Toll-like receptor 2 ligand that survives pasteurization.

evidence.snippet: Increasing evidence from human population studies and animal research has established correlative as well as causative links between chronic inflammation and insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Establishes both correlative and causative links between chronic inflammation and insulin resistance in obesity.

evidence.snippet: We propose that obesity-related insulin resistance is, at least in part, a chronic inflammatory disease initiated in adipose tissue.
evidence.explanation: Proposes that obesity-induced insulin resistance represents a chronic inflammatory disease originating in adipose tissue.

evidence.snippet: Particularly chronic inflammation in adipose tissue seems to play an important role in the development of obesity-related insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Highlights the central role of chronic adipose tissue inflammation in obesity-related insulin resistance.

steps/11.description: Systemic inflammation from adipose tissue contributes to insulin resistance, cardiovascular disease, and other complications. Elevated CRP, IL-6, and TNF-alpha levels.

evidence.snippet: we observed that treatment with pasteurized A. muciniphila increased energy excretion in the feces
evidence.explanation: The absorption step is inferred from its modification: treatment shifts energy from absorption to excretion, so the untreated state absorbs more.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrated that this effect was not due to the modulation of intestinal lipid absorption or chylomicron synthesis but likely involved a reduction of carbohydrates absorption and enhanced intestinal epithelial turnover
evidence.explanation: Localizes the effect to carbohydrate absorption and epithelial turnover rather than to lipid handling.

steps/12.description: The share of ingested energy that is absorbed rather than excreted in feces is a determinant of energy balance that sits upstream of adipose expansion. In diet-induced obese mice, pasteurized A. muciniphila lowers food energy efficiency and raises fecal energy excretion, apparently through reduced carbohydrate absorption and faster intestinal epithelial turnover, implying that the untreated state retains a correspondingly larger fraction of ingested energy.

evidence.snippet: Leptin is a mediator of long-term regulation of energy balance, suppressing food intake and thereby inducing weight loss. Ghrelin on the other hand is a fast-acting hormone, seemingly playing a role in meal initiation.
evidence.explanation: Describes the role of leptin and ghrelin as key hormones regulating energy balance in obesity.

evidence.snippet: In obese subjects the circulating level of the anorexigenic hormone leptin is increased, whereas surprisingly, the level of the orexigenic hormone ghrelin is decreased. It is now established that obese patients are leptin-resistant.
evidence.explanation: Explains the paradox of elevated leptin levels in obesity with concurrent leptin resistance, contributing to failed energy balance restoration.

steps/13.description: Chronic positive energy balance from excess caloric intake relative to expenditure leads to fat accumulation. Multiple regulatory systems (leptin, ghrelin, insulin) fail to restore balance.

evidence.snippet: we show that weight loss-induced variations in cellular stress, extracellular matrix remodelling, inflammatory responses, adipokine secretion and lipolysis seem to be associated with the amount of weight that is regained after successful weight loss
evidence.explanation: Synthesis of the human adipose-tissue responses associated with how much weight is regained. It is a review's synthesis of work it did not perform, hence quote_role REVIEW_SYNTHESIS.

evidence.snippet: Mice carrying this obesogenic memory show accelerated rebound weight gain
evidence.explanation: Shows the adipose memory is not merely correlative: animals carrying it regain weight faster. The corresponding human data in the same study are transcriptional rather than an observed regain rate.

steps/14.description: After energy restriction the body defends its previous mass through a coordinated set of responses: resting energy expenditure falls disproportionately to fat-free mass, anorexigenic signals fall while orexigenic signals rise, and shrinking adipocytes generate extracellular-matrix stress and immune activation in subcutaneous adipose tissue. Adipose tissue additionally retains a transcriptional and epigenetic memory of the prior obese state that primes it for accelerated regain. This node, rather than weight loss itself, is what maintenance therapy targets.

edges/4.description: Fewer mucus-resident Akkermansia is associated with a thinner mucus layer and a more permeable epithelium in rodent models of diet-induced obesity.

edges/5.description: Circulating lipopolysaccharide engages innate immune receptors and sustains the systemic inflammatory tone already established in expanded adipose tissue.

edges/6.description: Energy retained rather than excreted adds to the positive balance that drives fat accumulation.

edges/7.description: Regain restores the adiposity phenotype that the weight-loss phase reduced.

evidence.snippet: participants gaining 0.9 ± 0.3 kg (p = 0.009) during the ultra-processed diet and losing 0.9 ± 0.3 kg (p = 0.007) during the unprocessed diet
evidence.explanation: Inpatient randomised crossover trial in which the excess intake and weight gain are attributable to food processing itself rather than nutrient composition. This is direct experimental support for the energy-imbalance node.

edges/8.description: Ultra-processed diets drive excess energy intake and weight gain even when calories presented, energy density and macronutrients are matched.

evidence.snippet: the number of and distance to unhealthy food outlets increased the likelihood of fast-food consumption and higher BMI for children of any SES
evidence.explanation: Systematic review restricted to causal-inference studies. The environment acts through consumption and the energy-imbalance node rather than on body mass directly, and the BMI effect is established for children of any socioeconomic status but among adults only for selected groups.

edges/9.description: Density of and proximity to unhealthy food outlets raises fast-food consumption and body mass index.

evidence.snippet: The 16% of adults who are homozygous for the risk allele weighed about 3 kilograms more and had 1.67-fold increased odds of obesity when compared with those not inheriting a risk allele.
evidence.explanation: Large genome-wide association study establishing the common FTO variant as a robust risk factor for higher BMI and obesity.

genes/0.notes: The strongest common-variant association with body mass index. FTO acts as a susceptibility locus rather than a Mendelian cause: homozygotes for the risk allele carry a 1.67-fold increased odds of obesity, so the effect is a shift in population risk rather than a sufficient cause. No pathophysiology node in this entry models the FTO mechanism, so the gene is deliberately not bound to one.

evidence.snippet: While POMC deficiency is very rare, 1-5% of severely obese individuals harbor heterozygous mutations in MC4R.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the contribution of heterozygous MC4R variants to severe obesity. Graded BACKGROUND because the sentence is the framing of a setmelanotide trial rather than that trial's own result.

genes/1.notes: Heterozygous MC4R variants are carried by 1-5% of severely obese individuals and act here as a risk factor rather than a sufficient cause. Receptor-level MC4R deficiency as a monogenic disease in its own right is curated as the MC4R subtype of Obesity_Due_to_MC4R_Pathway_Disruption.

evidence.snippet: The severe obesity found in these congenitally leptin-deficient subjects provides the first genetic evidence that leptin is an important regulator of energy balance in humans.
evidence.explanation: First human evidence that a homozygous LEP frameshift mutation causes severe early-onset obesity via leptin deficiency.

genes/2.notes: Biallelic LEP loss of function is a rare monogenic cause of severe early-onset obesity, curated in full as Congenital_Leptin_Deficiency.

evidence.snippet: The prevalence of pathogenic LEPR mutations in a cohort of subjects with severe, early-onset obesity was 3%.
evidence.explanation: Establishes how much of severe early-onset obesity biallelic LEPR deficiency accounts for in a systematically screened cohort.

genes/3.notes: Biallelic LEPR variants are a rare monogenic cause of severe early-onset obesity, curated as the LEPR subtype of Obesity_Due_to_MC4R_Pathway_Disruption.

evidence.snippet: Rare homozygous or biallelic variants in POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR can disrupt signaling through the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) pathway, resulting in hyperphagia and severe early-onset obesity.
evidence.explanation: Supports POMC as a causative gene acting through the melanocortin-4 receptor pathway in severe early-onset obesity.

genes/4.notes: Biallelic POMC variants remove the melanocortin ligand input to MC4R and are a rare monogenic cause of severe early-onset obesity, curated as the POMC subtype of Obesity_Due_to_MC4R_Pathway_Disruption.

evidence.snippet: Significant weight loss was observed with any low-carbohydrate or low-fat diet.
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis of randomized trials showing dietary lifestyle modification produces significant weight loss in overweight and obese adults.

treatments/0.description: Dietary changes and increased physical activity as foundation of treatment.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Reducing energy intake and raising expenditure acts directly on the energy balance node. The link is definitional rather than empirical, so it carries no evidence of its own; the treatment's efficacy evidence is on the treatment itself.

evidence.snippet: In participants with overweight or obesity, 2.4 mg of semaglutide once weekly plus lifestyle intervention was associated with sustained, clinically relevant reduction in body weight.
evidence.explanation: STEP 1 randomized trial demonstrating substantial, sustained weight loss with the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide in obesity.

evidence.snippet: Strong recommendations were made for bupropion-naltrexone, semaglutide, tirzepatide, and setmelanotide, with moderate-certainty evidence.
evidence.explanation: The joint TOS/OMA/OAC pharmacological-management guidance makes a strong recommendation for semaglutide (a GLP-1 receptor agonist) for adults with obesity.

treatments/1.description: Semaglutide, liraglutide provide substantial weight loss through central appetite suppression and metabolic effects.

evidence.snippet: Semaglutide was associated with less hunger and food cravings, better control of eating and a lower preference for high-fat foods.
evidence.explanation: Mechanism-of-action crossover trial measuring the appetite and food-reward changes this node describes.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: GLP-1 receptor agonism acts on central appetite and food-reward circuits, restoring the satiety signalling that leptin resistance has blunted.

evidence.snippet: ad libitum energy intake was substantially lower with semaglutide vs placebo with a corresponding loss of body weight observed with semaglutide
evidence.explanation: Directly measures energy intake, the quantity the Energy Imbalance node is about.

treatments/1/targets/1.description: The appetite effect converts into a measured reduction in ad libitum energy intake, which is what moves the energy balance node.

evidence.snippet: participants regained two-thirds of their prior weight loss, with similar changes in cardiometabolic variables
evidence.explanation: That regain resumes on withdrawal establishes that the treatment had been acting on this node. Graded INDIRECT because the suppression is inferred from what happens when the drug is stopped.

treatments/1/targets/2.description: Suppression of regain is contingent on continued dosing: in the STEP 1 off-treatment extension participants regained two-thirds of their lost weight within a year of stopping, and cardiometabolic gains reverted with it. The drug holds the regain node down rather than resolving it.

evidence.snippet: In this 72-week trial in participants with obesity, 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg of tirzepatide once weekly provided substantial and sustained reductions in body weight.
evidence.explanation: SURMOUNT-1 randomized trial showing the GLP-1/GIP dual agonist tirzepatide produces substantial, sustained weight loss in obesity.

evidence.snippet: Strong recommendations were made for bupropion-naltrexone, semaglutide, tirzepatide, and setmelanotide, with moderate-certainty evidence.
evidence.explanation: The joint TOS/OMA/OAC pharmacological-management guidance makes a strong recommendation for tirzepatide (a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist) for adults with obesity.

treatments/2.description: Tirzepatide offers enhanced weight loss of 15-25% through dual incretin receptor activation.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonism reduces energy intake and produces sustained weight reduction. No tirzepatide-specific energy-intake measurement is cited here, so the link carries no evidence of its own.

evidence.snippet: In participants with obesity or overweight, withdrawing tirzepatide led to substantial regain of lost weight, whereas continued treatment maintained and augmented initial weight reduction.
evidence.explanation: A randomized withdrawal trial whose endpoint is weight-loss maintenance, which is this node.

treatments/2/targets/1.description: SURMOUNT-4 is a randomized withdrawal design and so measures this node directly: after a 36-week lead-in, participants switched to placebo regained weight while those continuing treatment did not.

evidence.snippet: As compared with conventional therapy, bariatric surgery appears to be a viable option for the treatment of severe obesity, resulting in long-term weight loss, improved lifestyle, and, except for hypercholesterolemia, amelioration in risk factors that were elevated at baseline.
evidence.explanation: Swedish Obese Subjects study showing bariatric surgery produces durable weight loss and risk-factor improvement in severe obesity.

treatments/3.description: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, sleeve gastrectomy for severe obesity.

evidence.snippet: Compared with lean and obese controls, patients following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) had increased postprandial plasma PYY and GLP-1 favoring enhanced satiety.
evidence.explanation: Measures the gut-hormone change that acts on central satiety signalling.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Rerouting the gut alters the entero-hypothalamic endocrine axis: postprandial PYY and GLP-1 rise after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass but not after gastric banding producing equivalent weight loss, so the effect is anatomical rather than a consequence of having lost weight.

treatments/3/targets/1.description: Restriction plus the anorectic hormone profile lowers energy intake. Carried as a description rather than evidence because the cited trials measure weight and risk factors, not energy intake.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicated that CBT and BT are effective interventions for weight loss, and that successful weight loss requires more aggressive interventions such as BT or CBT than MC and UC.
evidence.explanation: Network meta-analysis of randomized trials placing CBT and behavioral therapy above usual and minimal care for weight loss. REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the pooled estimate synthesizes trials the authors did not run.

treatments/4.description: Cognitive behavioral therapy for eating behaviors.

evidence.snippet: Orlistat taken with an appropriate diet promotes clinically significant weight loss and reduces weight regain in obese patients over a 2-year period.
evidence.explanation: European Multicentre Orlistat randomized trial demonstrating the lipase inhibitor orlistat produces clinically significant weight loss in obese patients.

evidence.snippet: MR-O and Conv-O similarly increased fecal fat percentage from 3.8% to 13.5%, confirming pharmacodynamic equivalence.
evidence.explanation: Human pharmacodynamic measurement of the shift from absorption to fecal excretion that defines this node.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Gastrointestinal lipase inhibition blocks hydrolysis of dietary triglyceride, so ingested fat leaves in the stool instead of being absorbed. Orlistat and pasteurized A. muciniphila MucT both act on this node by unrelated routes: one blocks a digestive enzyme, the other is reported to reduce carbohydrate absorption and raise epithelial turnover.

evidence.snippet: During year 2, patients who continued with orlistat regained, on average, half as much weight as those patients switched to placebo
evidence.explanation: Second-year maintenance result, measuring regain directly.

treatments/5/targets/1.description: The European Multicentre trial's second year is a maintenance phase, in which continuing orlistat halved the regain seen after switching to placebo.

evidence.snippet: 84 (16%) participants assigned to placebo had a decrease in bodyweight of 5% or more compared with 226 (48%) assigned to naltrexone 32 mg plus bupropion
evidence.explanation: COR-I co-primary endpoint, the proportion achieving at least 5% weight loss.

evidence.snippet: Strong recommendations were made for bupropion-naltrexone, semaglutide, tirzepatide, and setmelanotide, with moderate-certainty evidence.
evidence.explanation: The joint TOS/OMA/OAC guidance makes a strong recommendation for bupropion-naltrexone for adults with obesity.

treatments/6.description: Fixed-dose sustained-release naltrexone plus bupropion, developed to act on two complementary central pathways: bupropion stimulates hypothalamic POMC neurons, and naltrexone blocks the opioid-mediated autoinhibitory feedback that otherwise limits that stimulation. Approved for chronic weight management and strongly recommended in the joint TOS/OMA/OAC guidance already cited elsewhere in this entry.

evidence.snippet: Combination treatment with sustained-release naltrexone and bupropion was developed to produce complementary actions in CNS pathways regulating bodyweight.
evidence.explanation: States the central mechanism the combination was designed around. It is the trial's framing of prior pharmacology rather than a result of the trial, so it is graded BACKGROUND and OTHER, and bears on the node only indirectly.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: Both components act on central circuits regulating body weight rather than on peripheral energy handling, which is what places this treatment on the hypothalamic node.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, the MucT group had a greater net weight loss from baseline to end of maintenance than the placebo group (3.1 ± 0.7 kg, P = 0.009).
evidence.explanation: Net weight loss from baseline to the end of maintenance, the secondary anthropometric outcome.

evidence.snippet: No serious adverse events related to the treatment were observed.
evidence.explanation: Safety outcome of the 24-week maintenance trial.

evidence.snippet: Compared to placebo, pasteurized A. muciniphila improved insulin sensitivity
evidence.explanation: The earlier proof-of-concept human trial in metabolic syndrome, which found the metabolic signal without a significant weight effect on an unchanged ad libitum diet.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrated that daily oral supplementation of 1010 A. muciniphila bacteria either live or pasteurized for three months was safe and well tolerated
evidence.explanation: First-in-human safety and tolerability of the supplementation route used here.

treatments/7.description: Daily oral capsules of pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila MucT (heat-treated 30 minutes at 70 C; 3 x 10^10 inactivated cells per capsule) taken during the weight maintenance phase that follows a low-energy diet. Heat inactivation removes the oxygen sensitivity and manufacturing constraints of the live organism while preserving the thermostable outer-membrane protein Amuc_1100, and in rodents it increased rather than abolished the metabolic benefit. The indication tested is maintenance of weight already lost, not weight loss itself.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that MucT led to lower body weight regain versus placebo at the end of the weight maintenance period (MucT: 1.2 ± 0.7 kg, placebo: 3.2 ± 0.4 kg, P = 0.012).
evidence.explanation: Primary outcome of the randomized trial, stating the effect on the targeted mechanism.

treatments/7/targets/0.description: The registered primary outcome. Over 24 weeks of ad libitum healthy diet after an 8-week low-energy diet, the supplemented group regained less weight than placebo and ended with greater net weight loss from baseline.

evidence.snippet: We confirmed that daily oral administration of pasteurized A. muciniphila alleviated diet-induced obesity and decreased food energy efficiency.
evidence.explanation: Shows the treatment acts on how efficiently ingested energy is retained.

treatments/7/targets/1.description: Proposed mechanism: a shift of ingested energy from absorption to fecal excretion. Established in diet-induced obese mice; in the human trial the increase in fecal energy content did not reach significance, and only the within-group inverse association with weight change supported it.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrated that Amuc_1100, a specific protein isolated from the outer membrane of A. muciniphila, interacts with Toll-like receptor 2, is stable at temperatures used for pasteurization, improves the gut barrier and partly recapitulates the beneficial effects of the bacterium.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the barrier-directed mechanism and that it survives pasteurization.

treatments/7/targets/2.description: Proposed mechanism: the thermostable outer-membrane protein Amuc_1100 signals through TLR2 and improves gut barrier function, which is the route by which a non-viable preparation can act on host metabolism without colonizing.

evidence.snippet: The predominant mechanism for PGS×C is the amplification of genetic effects in adverse contexts, such as low polyunsaturated fatty acids or social determinants of ill health
evidence.explanation: Direct source (Nagpal & Gibson 2026): across seven UK Biobank diseases and 75 contexts, amplification of genetic effects in adverse contexts is identified as the predominant mechanism of PGS×context interaction — the mechanism applied in this hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: GxSex is pervasive but acts primarily through systematic sex differences in the magnitude of many genetic effects
evidence.explanation: Corroborates amplification — systematic differences in the magnitude of polygenic effects rather than in the identity of causal variants — as the primary mode of gene-by-context interaction.

hypotheses/0.description: Polygenic-score-by-context (PGS×C) interactions reported for obesity in the UK Biobank appear to reflect amplification rather than context-specific causal variants: the same susceptibility loci (e.g. FTO, MC4R, and other appetite/CNS-acting variants) exert systematically larger effects in disease-promoting contexts. This entry proposes that the amplification arises because polygenic liability and adverse exposures — obesogenic diet, physical inactivity, alcohol intake and socioeconomic deprivation — converge on the shared Energy Imbalance node, so their joint effect on the liability-threshold scale is super-additive rather than additive. Nagpal & Gibson (Nat Genet 2026, PMID:42443528) show amplifying context pairs for BMI-defined obesity (e.g. glucose with omega-3 fatty acids, and walking pace with beer intake) and note that the major contexts differ between BMI- and waist-to-hip-ratio definitions, consistent with BMI polymorphisms acting on central appetite regulation versus WHR variants acting on peripheral metabolic traits.

open_questions/0.rationale: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. For obesity this is acute for the biochemical "contexts": leptin and fasting insulin rise as a consequence of increased fat mass and are modelled in this entry as readouts of adipose dysfunction rather than upstream drivers, and reduced physical activity or slower walking pace may be consequences of established obesity rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled lifestyle interventions would actually reduce risk.

evidence.snippet: Initial Akkermansia spp. abundance was associated with cardiometabolic response to MucT.
evidence.explanation: States the baseline-abundance dependence that this gap is about.

evidence.snippet: AKK-WST01 supplementation showed high colonization efficiency and significant reductions in body weight, fat mass, and HbA1c, which were not found in the placebo group.
evidence.explanation: Independent trial of a live preparation showing the same restriction of benefit to participants with low baseline abundance.

open_questions/1.rationale: Two independent trials of different preparations point the same way. In the weight-maintenance trial (PMID:42120725) participants stratified below the median fecal A. muciniphila level after weight loss regained less weight and improved more in insulin sensitivity, blood pressure and fecal energy content than those above it, with no such split in the placebo arm; that analysis was exploratory and post hoc. In a separate trial of live AKK-WST01 in overweight/obese type 2 diabetes (PMID:39879980), benefit and colonization were likewise confined to the low-baseline group. If this holds prospectively it makes baseline abundance a pre-treatment stratifier rather than an incidental covariate, and it would change how a maintenance trial is powered and who is enrolled. The competing readings are not distinguished by the current data: greater room for improvement in depleted individuals, versus a resident community in high-abundance individuals that resists an added preparation. Note the mechanism cannot simply be colonization for the pasteurized product, which is non-viable.

steps/0.description: Y. pestis reaches the lung either directly through inhaled infectious respiratory droplets or secondarily through hematogenous spread from another infected focus, establishing pulmonary infection rather than the draining-lymph-node or primary bloodstream forms of plague.

evidence.snippet: Pla allows Y. pestis to replicate rapidly in the airways, causing a lethal fulminant pneumonia
evidence.explanation: Shows that Pla is an airway-replication determinant of primary pneumonic plague.

steps/1.description: The Y. pestis plasminogen activator Pla is required for primary pneumonic plague and permits rapid airway replication rather than inflammatory clearance and lung repair.

evidence.snippet: Yersinia pestis, the etiologic agent of plague, utilizes a type III secretion system (T3SS) to subvert the defenses of its mammalian hosts.
evidence.explanation: Establishes T3SS-mediated evasion of mammalian host defenses, the shared Y. pestis virulence machinery active after pulmonary infection.

evidence.snippet: several Yop effectors secreted through the T3SS effectively inhibit this host response
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that T3SS-delivered Yop effectors suppress leukotriene B4-mediated early inflammatory signaling by leukocytes.

evidence.snippet: LcrV signals in a CD14- and toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2)-dependent fashion leading to immunosuppression by interleukin 10 induction
evidence.explanation: Identifies LcrV as an inducer of IL-10-mediated innate immune suppression.

evidence.snippet: F1 and the virulence plasmid-encoded type III system act in concert to make Y. pestis highly resistant to uptake by phagocytes.
evidence.explanation: Shows that the F1 capsule and the T3SS cooperate to inhibit phagocytic uptake of Y. pestis.

steps/2.description: During the first 24 to 36 hours in the lung, Y. pestis combines Yop delivery, LcrV-induced IL-10 signaling, and F1 capsule-mediated antiphagocytosis to delay leukocyte recruitment and suppress innate inflammatory control.

evidence.snippet: begins with an antiinflammatory state in the first 24-36 h that rapidly progresses to a highly proinflammatory state by 48 h
evidence.explanation: Establishes the biphasic inflammatory trajectory of primary pneumonic plague.

evidence.snippet: Some of these immunogenic proteins as well as the capsular antigen F1 are exploited for diagnostic purposes, which are critical in the context of the rapid onset of death in the absence of antibiotic treatment (less than a week for bubonic plague and <48 h for pneumonic plague).
evidence.explanation: Places pneumonic plague diagnosis in the context of death within less than 48 hours without antibiotic treatment.

steps/3.description: The initially anti-inflammatory pulmonary infection rapidly flips to a highly pro-inflammatory phase with purulent multifocal exudative bronchopneumonia, alveolar injury, bloody sputum, and clinical pneumonia.

evidence.snippet: unrestricted bacterial replication in lymph nodes (bubonic plague) and in lungs (pneumonic plague)
evidence.explanation: The pneumonic form is the lung-infection form of plague.

evidence.snippet: unrestricted bacterial replication in lymph nodes (bubonic plague) and in lungs (pneumonic plague)
evidence.explanation: Links bacterial replication in lung tissue to the pneumonic form.

edges/0.description: Temperature-induced virulence factors enable Y. pestis to replicate rapidly in the airways after lung seeding.

edges/1.description: Pla-supported airway replication amplifies the bacterial population during the early anti-inflammatory phase of pneumonic plague.

edges/2.description: Delayed early inflammation permits unchecked pulmonary bacterial growth before bacterial burden triggers an abrupt pro-inflammatory lung-injury phase.

edges/3.description: Infection of the lung manifests clinically as pneumonia.

edges/4.description: Fulminant pneumonia can produce bloody sputum and hemoptysis.

edges/5.description: Exudative bronchopneumonia produces shortness of breath.

edges/6.description: Pulmonary inflammation and airway exudate produce cough.

edges/7.description: Fulminant lower-respiratory infection can cause chest pain.

edges/8.description: The abrupt pro-inflammatory phase produces systemic fever.

edges/9.description: Rapid pulmonary Y. pestis proliferation can progress to bacteremia and systemic septic complications.

edges/10.description: Severe septicemic plague can trigger consumptive coagulopathy as a terminal complication.

evidence.snippet: the rapid onset of death in the absence of antibiotic treatment (less than a week for bubonic plague and <48 h for pneumonic plague)
evidence.explanation: Documents the characteristic rapidity and lethality of untreated pneumonic plague.

edges/11.description: Severe exudative bronchopneumonia can progress to respiratory failure.

evidence.snippet: In addition to aminoglycosides, other classes of antimicrobials including tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, and sulfonamides are effective for plague treatment
evidence.explanation: Systematic review of individual treated human plague cases identifying several active antibiotic classes.

evidence.snippet: Mortality differed significantly among those receiving high-efficacy therapy (9%) and only limited-efficacy therapy (51%).
evidence.explanation: Public-health surveillance associates early high-efficacy antimicrobial therapy with markedly improved survival in human plague.

treatments/0.description: Antimicrobial treatment must be started early because the pneumonic form can be fatal within 48 hours without therapy; aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, and sulfonamides all have reported clinical activity in treated human plague.

evidence.snippet: Rickettsia spp. DNA was detected in capillary blood from both lesions, and sequencing of the PCR amplicons identified R. helvetica
evidence.explanation: Lesion-focused PCR after Ixodes attachment detected R. helvetica DNA at bite-associated skin lesions, supporting local inoculation.

steps/0.description: An infected tick introduces R. helvetica into skin during attachment, seeding a local lesion that can contain rickettsial DNA and, in some patients, necrose into an inoculation eschar.

evidence.snippet: One of the initial targets for rickettsiae after inoculation by ticks is the macrophage/monocyte.
evidence.explanation: This frames the in-vitro R. helvetica monocyte experiment at the inoculation-to-endothelium step in rickettsial pathogenesis.

evidence.snippet: R. helvetica survives and propagates in the THP-1 cells.
evidence.explanation: Human THP-1 monocytic cells supported R. helvetica survival and propagation in vitro.

evidence.snippet: Infected monocytes induced TNF-α which may be important in host defence against rickettsial infections and promote cell survival and inhibiting cell death by apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Infected monocytes initiated a TNF-alpha inflammatory program, supporting the node's link to early inflammatory signaling.

steps/1.description: In the early post-inoculation phase, monocytes/macrophages can be exposed before vascular endothelial infection is established. In a THP-1 human monocytic model, R. helvetica survived, propagated, and induced TNF-alpha, supporting monocytes as an early host-cell compartment in the pathograph.

evidence.snippet: Residing free in the cytosol of the host cell, they acquire many necessary components via transport mechanisms instead of maintaining genes for synthesizing sugars, lipids, nucleotides, and amino acids.
evidence.explanation: The rickettsial pathogenesis review supports the free cytosolic niche as the conserved intracellular lifestyle of Rickettsia species.

steps/2.description: Like pathogenic Rickettsia generally, R. helvetica is modeled as a cytosolic intracellular bacterium; this niche places the organism beyond extracellular-only antibacterial exposure and requires cell-penetrant therapy.

evidence.snippet: The ribosome is one of the main antibiotic targets in the bacterial cell.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence establishes the bacterial ribosome as the conserved target of tetracycline-class therapy; the R. helvetica-specific treatment evidence below establishes doxycycline responsiveness in human disease.

steps/3.description: R. helvetica requires bacterial 70S ribosomal translation to synthesize proteins; doxycycline reaches intracellular rickettsiae and blocks the 30S ribosomal subunit.

evidence.snippet: All patients showed a four-fold increase in antibody titer to the spotted fever rickettsia, R. helvetica, and immunohistochemical examination revealed rickettsia-like organisms in the walls of skin capillaries and veins.
evidence.explanation: R. helvetica-seroconverting human cases had rickettsia-like organisms in skin capillary and venous walls, directly anchoring the endothelial small-vessel lesion.

evidence.snippet: The fundamental lesion of rickettsial diseases is vasculitis
evidence.explanation: Review synthesis supports small-vessel vasculitis as the shared rickettsial tissue lesion downstream of endothelial infection.

steps/4.description: Spotted-fever-group rickettsiae disseminate from the bite site and target microvascular endothelium, producing focal small-vessel vasculitis; in R. helvetica infection this conserved mechanism is kept narrow because most reported human disease is mild and aneruptive.

evidence.snippet: Examination of PCR-positive tissue showed chronic interstitial inflammation and the presence of rickettsia-like organisms predominantly located in the endothelium.
evidence.explanation: In fatal chronic perimyocarditis cases with R. helvetica DNA, inflamed PCR-positive tissue contained endothelium-localized rickettsia-like organisms.

steps/5.description: Rare disseminated R. helvetica infection can involve pericardial, coronary, and myocardial tissue, with chronic interstitial inflammation and endothelium-localized rickettsia-like organisms in reported sudden-cardiac death cases.

evidence.snippet: Most reports of human exposure have described asymptomatic seroconversion or a mild, self-limiting flu-like illness but it has also been implicated as a cause of subacute lymphocytic meningitis.
evidence.explanation: The retrospective Danish study summarizes the published neurologic association and places lymphocytic meningitis outside the usual mild flu-like presentation.

steps/6.description: R. helvetica has been implicated as a cause of subacute lymphocytic meningitis, defining a rare neurologic branch of disease while leaving the intervening CNS trafficking and inflammatory steps unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms included fever, headache, and arthralgia in all patients, myalgia in four, and an inoculation eschar in one but no cutaneous rash.
evidence.explanation: The eight-patient serologic case series identifies fever as part of the dominant mild aneruptive presentation.

steps/7.description: Fever is the cardinal systemic manifestation of R. helvetica infection.

evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms included fever, headache, and arthralgia in all patients, myalgia in four, and an inoculation eschar in one but no cutaneous rash.
evidence.explanation: The serologic case series places headache in the dominant R. helvetica symptom complex.

steps/8.description: Headache accompanies the acute febrile syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms included fever, headache, and arthralgia in all patients, myalgia in four, and an inoculation eschar in one but no cutaneous rash.
evidence.explanation: Four of the European serologically supported patients had myalgia.

steps/9.description: Myalgia is part of the nonspecific flu-like syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms included fever, headache, and arthralgia in all patients, myalgia in four, and an inoculation eschar in one but no cutaneous rash.
evidence.explanation: Arthralgia was reported in the European serologically supported R. helvetica cases.

steps/10.description: Arthralgia can accompany the acute R. helvetica febrile illness.

evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms included fever, headache, and arthralgia in all patients, myalgia in four, and an inoculation eschar in one but no cutaneous rash.
evidence.explanation: The series recorded an inoculation eschar in only one patient, supporting eschar as possible rather than typical for R. helvetica infection.

steps/11.description: A necrotic eschar can occur at the infected tick attachment site, although it was uncommon in the small published case series.

evidence.snippet: In the present case, however, where the presence of R. helvetica in the blood was verified by PCR together with serologic evidence of infection, the patient presented a different clinical picture with acute febrile illness, rash and long-lasting myasthenia.
evidence.explanation: A bacteremic PCR- and serology-supported case shows that R. helvetica can present with rash despite the usual aneruptive pattern.

steps/12.description: R. helvetica is often described as aneruptive, but PCR- and serology-supported bacteremic disease can include rash.

evidence.snippet: We studied two young Swedish men who died of sudden cardiac failure during exercise, and who showed signs of perimyocarditis similar to those described in rickettsial disease.
evidence.explanation: The case report ties R. helvetica infection to fatal chronic perimyocarditis in two young men.

steps/13.description: Chronic perimyocarditis with R. helvetica DNA in cardiac tissue has been reported in sudden cardiac death.

evidence.snippet: Most reports of human exposure have described asymptomatic seroconversion or a mild, self-limiting flu-like illness but it has also been implicated as a cause of subacute lymphocytic meningitis.
evidence.explanation: The Danish study cites subacute lymphocytic meningitis as a published severe neurologic presentation of R. helvetica infection.

steps/14.description: R. helvetica has been implicated in subacute lymphocytic meningitis.

edges/0.description: Tick inoculation can expose early macrophage and monocyte targets to viable rickettsiae.

edges/1.description: Bite-site infection can produce a necrotic eschar.

edges/3.description: Systemic rickettsial spread can extend infection to microvascular endothelium.

edges/4.description: Cytosolic R. helvetica remains dependent on bacterial ribosomal protein synthesis.

edges/5.description: Endotheliotropic infection and inflammatory signaling drive systemic fever.

edges/6.description: Systemic inflammation can present as headache.

edges/7.description: Systemic inflammation can present as myalgia.

edges/8.description: Systemic inflammation can present as arthralgia.
